Like it: ﴿وَلَوْ تَرَى إِذِ المُجْرِمُونَ﴾, ﴿وَلَوْ تَرَى الذِينَ ظَلَمُوا﴾, and His saying in al-Zumar: ﴿أَمْ مَنْ هُوَ قَانِتٌ آنَاءَ اللَّيْلِ سَاجداً وقَائِماً يَحْذَرُ الآخِرَةَ وَيَرْجُو رَحْمَةَ رَبِّهِ﴾, and no answer was given for it; His saying ﴿قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِى الَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُونَ وَالَّذِينَ لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ sufficed for it. So this is among the things whose answer is left out and what follows suffices for it. Likewise He said in Hūd: ﴿مَثَلُ الْفَرِيقَيْنِ كَالأَعْمَى وَالأصَمِّ وَالْبَصِيرِ وَالسَّمِيعِ هَلْ يَسْتَوِيَانِ مَثَلاً﴾ and did not say «هل يستوون» ("are they [plural] equal"). That is because the blind and the deaf are the description of one, and the seeing and the hearing are the description of one, as a speaker says: "I passed by the intelligent and the sensible man," meaning one person. The poet said:
وما أدرى إذا يمَّمت وجهاً * أريد الخير أيُّهما يلينى
أألخير الذى أنا أَبتغيه * أم الشر الذى لا يأتلينى
(I do not know, when I set out in some direction seeking good, which of the two will befall me: the good that I seek, or the evil that never fails to seek me.)
He said «أيّهما» ("which of the two") though he mentioned only the good, because the meaning is known: one who seeks good is guarding against evil. Likewise the saying of Allah, exalted be His mention: ﴿سَرَابِيلَ تَقِيكُم الْحَرَّ وَسَرَابِيلَ تَقِيكُمْ بَأْسَكُمْ﴾ [that is,] and they protect from the cold. It is so even though it is not mentioned.
His saying: ﴿وَمَن يَكْفُرْ بِهِ مِنَ ٱلأَحْزَابِ فَٱلنَّارُ مَوْعِدُهُ﴾: it is said [it means] of the kinds of unbelievers. And it is said that every unbeliever is a faction (ḥizb).

farraa:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لَهُمْ مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مِنْ أَوْلِيَآءَ يُضَاعَفُ لَهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ﴾: then the heads of the unbelievers who lead astray. His saying: ﴿مَا كَانُواْ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ ٱلسَّمْعَ﴾ has two interpretations. Some exegetes explained it: the punishment is doubled for them because they were able to hear and did not do so. In that case the bāʾ ought to have entered, since He said: ﴿وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ بِمَا كَانُوا يَكْذِبُونَ﴾ — in more than one place in the Revelation the bāʾ has been brought in — but its omission is permissible, as you say in speech: «بأَحسن ما كانوا يعملون» and «وأحسنَ ما كانوا يعملون». And you say in speech: «لأجزينَّك بما عملت» and «وما عملت» ("I will surely repay you for what you did"). And it is said [the second interpretation]: they were not able to hear and they did not see, that is, Allah led them astray from that in the Preserved Tablet.

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ جَرَمَ أَنَّهُمْ﴾. It is an expression that was originally equivalent to «لا بُدَّ أنّك قائم» ("there is no escaping that you are standing") and «لا محالة أَنّك ذاهب» ("inevitably you are going"); it ran on that pattern and their use of it became frequent until it came to mean «حقّا» ("truly"). Do you not see that the Arabs say: «لا جَرَم لآتينك» ("truly, I will come to you") and «لا جرم قد أحسنتَ» ("truly, you have done well")? And so the exegetes explained it in the sense of «الحقّ». Its origin is from «جَرَمت», that is, "I earned a sin," and «جَرَّمته». The saying of one who said that «جَرَمت» is like your saying «حَقُقت» or «حُقِقت» is of no account; the speaker was only confused by the saying of the poet:
ولقد طَعْنتُ أَبا عُيَيْنة طعنةً * جَرَمت فزارةُ بعدها أن تغضبا
(I dealt Abū ʿUyayna a thrust after which Fazāra were bound to be angry.)
They put (فَزارة) in the nominative and said: we make the verb belong to Fazāra, as if it were equivalent to «حُقَّ لها» or «حقَّ لها أن تغضب» ("it was right for her to be angry"). But «فَزارة» is accusative in the view of al-Farrāʾ, that is: the thrust brought upon them that they be angry.
Because of its frequency in speech, the mīm has been dropped from it, and the Banū Fazāra say: «لا جَرَ أَنك قائم». It is also joined at its beginning with «ذا»; one of the Banū Kilāb recited to me:
إن كلاباً والدِى لاذا جَرَمْ * لأَهْدِرَنَّ اليوم هدراً صادقا * هدر المعنَّى ذى الشقاشيق اللهِم *
(Kilāb is my father — truly, I shall roar today a true roar, the roar of a tethered stallion with frothing bladders, devouring.)
The position of «أنْ» is nominative, as in his saying:
أحقّا عبادَ الله جُرْأةُ مُحْلِقٍ * عَلَىَّ وقد أَعييتُ عادَ وتُبَّعا
(Is it true, O servants of Allah, that Muḥliq dares against me, when I have worn out ʿĀd and Tubbaʿ?)

farraa:23-23.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَخْبَتُوۤاْ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ﴾. Its meaning is: they humbled themselves for their Lord and towards their Lord. The Arabs sometimes put (إلى) in the place of the lām. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿بِأَنَّ رَبَّكَ أَوْحَى لَهَا﴾, and He said: ﴿الْحَمْدُ لِلّهِ الَّذِى هَدَانَا لِهَذَا﴾, and He said: ﴿يَهْدِيهِمْ إِلَيْه صِرَاطاً مُسْتَقِيماً﴾, and He said: ﴿فَأَوْحَى إِلَيْهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ﴾. It is permissible in Arabic to say: «فلان يُخبِت إلى الله», meaning: he does that with his face turned towards Allah; for the meaning of al-ikhbāt is humility, so he is saying: he does it with his face towards Allah and for Allah. The exegesis has come: «وأَخبتوا فَرَقا من الله» ("they humbled themselves out of fear of Allah"); so «مِن» resembles the meaning of the lām and the meaning of «إلى» when you intend by it "on account of this" and "because of this."

farraa:27-27.t:
His saying: ﴿مَا نَرَاكَ إِلاَّ بَشَراً مِّثْلَنَا وَمَا نَرَاكَ ٱتَّبَعَكَ إِلاَّ ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ أَرَاذِلُنَا﴾. You put «الأراذل» in the nominative by «الاتّباع» (the verb "follow"), while the [first] verb at the beginning of the speech has fallen on its own noun. The Arabs hardly ever make what is brought back by «إلاّ» refer to anything but the mubtadaʾ (the head noun), not to a pronoun referring back to it; yet it is permissible. The clear case about which there is no question is to say: «ما قام أحد إلاّ زيد» ("no one stood except Zayd"). If you say: «ما أحد قام إلا زيد», putting Zayd in the nominative by what refers back in the verb of «أحد», it is rare but permissible. It is remote [to relate it] to the mubtadaʾ only because it is a pronoun (kināya), and in a pronoun no distinction is made between «أحد» and «عبدالله»; since it is ugly to say «ما قام هو إلاّ زيد» ("he did not stand except Zayd") and good to say «ما قام أحد إلا زيد», that became clear, because «أحد» is as if it were not in the speech, so referring [the excepted noun] to the verb is good. And «أحد» is not said of a definite noun or a pronoun, since — resembling a definite noun — it is as if it were not in the speech. Do you not see that you say «ما مررت بأحد إلا بزيد» (so it is as if you said: «ما مررت إلا بزيد» "I passed by none but Zayd"), because «أحد» is not conceived in the mind as something aimed at? And it is ugly to say «ليس أحد مررت به إلاّ بزيد», because the hāʾ has a form like that of a definite noun, and you do not say «ما قمت إلا زيد»; this is the reason for its ugliness. Likewise He said (ما نراك), then it is as though He dropped (نراك) and said: (ما اتَّبعك إلا الذين هم أراذلنا). So build on this whatever comes to you, if Allah wills.
﴿بَادِيَ ٱلرَّأْيِ﴾: do not put a hamza in (بادى), because the meaning is "in what appears (yaẓhar) to us and becomes manifest (yabdū)." Were you to read (بادئ الرأى) with hamza, meaning "at first thought," it would be correct. Someone recited to me:
أضحى لخالى شبهى بادى بدى * وصار للفحل لسانى ويدى
(My likeness to my maternal uncle became apparent at first sight, and my tongue and my hand came to belong to the stallion.)
and he did not put a hamza. Like it is what the Arabs say in the sense of "begin with this first": then they say: «ابدأ بهذا آثراً مّا», «وآثِر ذى أثِير» («وأثير ذى أثير»), «وإثْرَ ذى أثير», «وابدأ بهذا أوَّل ذاتِ يدين» and «وأدْنَى دَنِىّ». And they recited to us:
فقالوا ما تريد فقلت ألهو * إلى الإصباح آثِر ذى أَثِير
(They said: What do you want? I said: To amuse myself until morning, before anything else.)
His saying: ﴿بَلْ نَظُنُّكُمْ كَاذِبِينَ﴾ is like His saying ﴿يأيّها النَّبِىُّ إِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساَء﴾, because they called Noah alone a liar, and it came out in the form of the plural; and His saying ﴿فَإنْ لَمْ يَسْتَجيبُوا لَكُمْ﴾: by «لكم» the Prophet ﷺ is meant. And His saying: ﴿فاعْلَمُوا﴾ is not for the Prophet ﷺ; it is only for the unbelievers of Mecca. Do you not see that He said ﴿فَهَلْ أَنْتُم مُسْلِمونَ﴾?

farraa:28-28.t:
His saying: ﴿وَآتَانِي رَحْمَةً مِّنْ عِندِهِ﴾.
It means the message (al-risāla); it is a favour and a mercy. His saying: ﴿فَعُمِّيَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read it [so]. In the reading of Ubayy it is (فعمَّاهَا عَلَيْكُمْ). I have heard the Arabs say: «قد عُمِّىَ علىَّ الخَبَر» and «عَمِىَ علىَّ» with one meaning ("the news was obscured to me"). This is one of the cases where the Arabs shifted the verb onto something to which it does not belong, it originally belonging to something else; do you not see that it is the man who is blind to the news, or is blinded to it? But in its permissibility it is like the Arabs' saying: «دخل الخاتمُ فى يدى والخُفّ فى رِجْلى» ("the ring entered my hand and the boot my foot"), while you know that it is the foot that is put into the boot and the finger into the ring. They took liberties with that because the meaning is known — it does not belong to this one at one time and to that one at another; it belongs only to one. So they allowed that for this reason. The general body of readers read it (فعَمِيَتْ). «[Translator's note: the printed text reads «قاستخفّوا», evidently for «فاستخفّوا» ("they took liberties").]»
His saying ﴿أَنُلْزِمُكُمُوهَا﴾: the Arabs make the mīm of «اللزوم» quiescent and say: «أَنُلْزِمْكُمُوهَا». That is because the vowels have come in succession, so the mīm was made quiescent because of its own vowel and two vowels after it, and because it is nominative [i.e. carries ḍamma]; were it accusative, it would not be felt heavy and lightened. They feel heavy only a kasra followed by a ḍamma, or a ḍamma followed by a kasra, or two kasras in succession, or two ḍammas in succession. As for the two ḍammas, it is His saying: ﴿لاَ يَحْزُنْهُمْ﴾: they made the nūn quiescent because there is a ḍamma before it, and it was lightened, as they say (رُسْل). As for the two kasras, it is like their saying «الإبلْ» when lightened. As for the ḍamma and the kasra, it is like the saying of the poet:
وناعٍ يُخَبِّرنا بمُهْلَك سَيّدٍ * تَقَطَّع من وجد عليه الأناملُ
(And a herald of death informing us of the death of a lord, for grief over whom fingertips are cut to pieces.)
and if you wish, «تُقطَّع». And his saying with the two kasras:
* إِذا اعوجَجْن قلت صَاحِبْ قوِّمِ *
(When they swerved I said: "Companion, set them straight!")
meaning «صَاحبى». Ḍamma and kasra are felt heavy only because their articulation costs effort for the tongue and lips: the lips are rounded for the rafʿ, so the ḍamma is heavy, and one side of the mouth is drawn towards the kasra, so you find that heavy; whereas the fatḥa comes out of the opening of the mouth without effort. «[Translator's note: the printed text reads «منصولة», evidently for «منصوبة» ("accusative"), and the phrase «أو يُسْتَثْقَل» appears to be a stray repetition; both are translated as intended.]»

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيٰقَوْمِ مَن يَنصُرُنِي مِنَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
He is saying: who will protect me from Allah? And likewise everything of this in the Qur'an: «النصر» is in the sense of protection.

farraa:35-35.t:
His saying: ﴿فَعَلَيَّ إِجْرَامِي﴾.
He is saying: then upon me is my sin. In the exegesis it has come as "then upon me are my sins," so if it were read «أجرامى» according to the exegesis, it would be correct. Abū al-Jarrāḥ recited to me:
لا تجعلونى كذوى الأجرام * الدَّهْمَسِيَّيْنِ ذوِى ضِرغام
(Do not make me like the men of crimes, the two secretive ones, the men of lion-like fierceness.)
So he pluralised «الجُرْم» as «أجرام». Like that is ﴿واللهُ يَعْلَمُ إِسْرَارَهُمْ﴾ and (أَسْراَرهم); it has been read both ways. Of it also is ﴿وَمِنَ اللّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ وإِدْبَارَ السُّجُودِ﴾ and (أَدْبَارَ السُّجُودِ). Whoever says (إِدْبَارَ) means the maṣdar (verbal noun), and whoever says (أسرار) means the plural of «السِّر».

farraa:36-36.t: His saying: ﴿فَلاَ تَبْتَئِسْ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَفْعَلُونَ﴾. He is saying: (do not be abased and do not grieve).

farraa:37-37.t: His saying: ﴿بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَوَحْيِنَا﴾ is like His saying ﴿ارْجِعُونِ﴾: it comes out in the plural while its meaning is singular, in line with what I explained to you of His saying ﴿بَلْ نَظُنُّكُمْ كاذِبِينَ﴾ [said] to Noah alone, and ﴿عَلَي خَوْفٍ مِنْ فِرْعَوْنَ وَمَلَئِهِمْ﴾.

farraa:40-40.t: His saying: ﴿وَفَارَ ٱلتَّنُّورُ﴾: it is the baker's oven. [The meaning is:] when water gushes up from the hottest place in your house, that is the sign of the punishment, so set out by night with your family. His saying ﴿مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ﴾: the male and the female of every kind are a pair. His saying ﴿وَأَهْلَكَ إِلاَّ مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقَوْلُ﴾: he carried with him a wife of his other than the one who perished, three sons and their wives, and eighty people besides. That is His saying ﴿وَمَنْ آمَنَ وَمَآ آمَنَ مَعَهُ إِلاَّ قَلِيلٌ﴾, and (the eighty) are the "few."

farraa:41-41.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقَالَ ٱرْكَبُواْ فِيهَا بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ ﴿إن شئت جَعلت مَجْرها ومَرْساها﴾ in the position of the nominative by the bāʾ, as you say: "its sailing and its anchoring are in the name of Allah and by the command of Allah." «[Translator's note: the printed text places «إن شئت جعلت مجرها ومرساها» inside Qur'anic brackets, though it is al-Farrāʾ's own wording ("if you wish, you may make «مجراها ومرساها»…"); translated as written.]» If you wish, you may make (بسم الله) a beginning sufficient in itself, like the saying of someone at slaughtering or at beginning a meal and the like: "In the name of Allah"; and (مجريها ومرسيها) is then in the position of the accusative, meaning: in the name of Allah at its sailing and at its anchoring. I have heard the Arabs say: «الحمد لله سِرَارَك وإِهلالك» ("praise be to Allah [from] your waning to your waxing"), and it has been heard from them: «الحمد لله ما إِهلالَك إِلى سرارك», meaning: between your crescent and your waning.
«المجرى» and «المرسى» — with ḍamma on both their mīms: Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, al-Ḥasan and the people of Medina read thus. Muḥammad related to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ related to us, saying: Abū Muʿāwiya related to us from al-Aʿmash, from Muslim ibn Ṣubayḥ, from Masrūq, that he read it (مَجْراها) with fatḥa on the mīm and (مُرسها) with ḍamma on the mīm. He said: And al-Farrāʾ related to us, saying: Abū Muʿāwiya and others related to us from al-Aʿmash, from a man whom he named, from ʿArfaja, that he heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd read it (مجراها) with fatḥa on the mīm and with ḍamma on the mīm of «مرسيها». Mujāhid read (مُجْرِيها ومُرسِيها), making it among the attributes of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; it is then in the position of the genitive (khafḍ) in i'rab, because it is definite. It may also be accusative, because the like of it may be indefinite, since the alif and lām fit well on both of them; do you not see that you say in speech: «بسم الله المجريها والمرسِيها»? When you remove the alif and lām from it, you put it in the accusative. What shows you its indefiniteness is His saying: ﴿هَذَا عَارِضٌ مُمْطِرُنَا﴾ and His saying: ﴿فَلَمّا رَأَوْهُ عَارِضاً مُسْتَقْبِلَ أَوْدِيَتِهِمْ﴾: they annexed it to a definite noun and made it the naʿt (adjective) of an indefinite noun. And the poet said:
يا رُبَّ عابِطنا لو كان يأْمُلكم * لا قى مباعدةً منكم وحرمانا
(Many a one who envies us, had he hoped in you, would have met with distance and deprivation from you.)
And another's saying:
وَيا رب هاجى مِنْقَرٍ يبتغى به * ليَكْرُم لمّا أعوزته المكارمُ
(And many a satirist of Minqar seeks thereby to be thought noble, when noble deeds have failed him.)
And al-Kisāʾī heard a Bedouin say after the breaking of the fast: «رُبّ صائمه لن يصومه وقائمه لن يقومه» ("many a one who fasted it will not fast it [again], and who prayed in it will not pray in it [again]").

farraa:43-43.t:
His saying: ﴿سَآوِيۤ إِلَىٰ جَبَلٍ يَعْصِمُنِي مِنَ ٱلْمَآءِ﴾. (قَالَ) Noah (peace be upon him): ﴿لاَعَاصِمَ اليَوْمَ مِنْ أمرِ الله إلاَّ مَنْ رَحِمَ﴾. «مَن» is in the position of the accusative, because the one protected is other than the protector, and the one shown mercy is protected; so it is as though he put it in the accusative in the manner of His saying ﴿مَالَهُمْ بِهِ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إلاَّ اتّباع الظَّنِّ﴾. Whoever permits the nominative of «الاتّباع», or the nominative in the poet's saying:
وبلدٍ ليس به أنيسُ * إلاَّ اليَعَافِيرُ وَإِلاَّ العِيسُ
(And many a land with no companion in it except gazelles and white camels.)
it is not permissible for him to use the nominative in (مَن), because the one who said (إلاّ اليعافيرُ) made the gazelles and wild beasts the companions of the desert; likewise His saying ﴿إلاَّ اتِّبَاع الظَّنِّ﴾ is saying: their knowledge is conjecture. But in no way may you say: the protected is the protector. However, if you took «العاصم» in the sense of «معصوم», as though you said: "there is none protected today from the command of Allah," the nominative of (مَن) would be permissible. Do not deny that the passive participle (mafʿūl) may come out in the form of the active (fāʿil); do you not see His saying ﴿مِنْ مَاءٍ دَافِقٍ﴾, whose meaning — and Allah knows best — is "poured out" (madfūq), and His saying ﴿فىِ عِيِشَةٍ رَاضِيَةٍ﴾, whose meaning is "pleasing" (marḍiyya)? And the poet said:
دعِ المكارمَ لا ترحل لِبُغيتها * واقعد فإنك أنت الطاعم الكاسى
(Leave noble deeds — do not travel in quest of them — and sit, for you are the one fed and clothed.)
Its meaning is «المكسوّ» ("the clothed"). You can deduce that from the fact that you say «رضيتُ هذه المعيشةَ» ("I was pleased with this life") but not «رَضِيَتْ» [of the life itself], and «دُفِق الماء» ("the water was poured out") but not «دَفَق», and you say «كُسِى العريان» ("the naked man was clothed") but not «كسا». It is also read (إلاّ من رُحِم). And had it been said «لا عاصم اليوم من أمر الله إلاّ من رُحِم», it would be as though you said: Allah does not protect today any but the one shown mercy; but we have not heard anyone read it so.

farraa:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱسْتَوَتْ عَلَى ٱلْجُودِيِّ﴾: it is a mountain at Ḥaḍanān in the land of Mosul; its yāʾ is doubled. I have been told that one of the readers read (عَلَى الجُودِى) with the yāʾ unstressed. If that is sound, it is among the words that were used much by its people and so were lightened; or it may have been named with a feminine verb form like «حُطىِّ», «أصِرّى» and «صَرِّى», and then the alif and lām were brought in. Someone recited to me — he was al-Mufaḍḍal —:
وكفرتَ قوماً هُمْ هَدَوكَ لأقدِمى * إِذا زَجْر أبيكَ سَأْسَاْ واربُق
(And you were ungrateful to a people who guided you to «أقدمي» ["go forward!"], when your father's urging [of his donkey] was "saʾsaʾ" and "irbuq.")
And one of the Banū Asad recited to me:
لمّا رأيت أنها فى حُطّى * وفَتكتْ فى كذبى ولَطِّى
(When I saw that she was in "ḥuṭṭī" and went to extremes in my lying and my concealing.)
When the Arabs make the like of «حُطّى» and its kin a name and want to change it away from the verbal pattern, they turn the yāʾ into alif and say: «حُطَّا», «أصِرَّا» and «صِرَّا». Likewise those Persian names ending in yāʾ, such as «ماهى», «شاهى» and «شُنىِّ», they turn into alif and say: «ماها», «شاها» and «شنَّا». Someone recited to us:
أتانا حِمَاسٌ بابن ماها يسوقه * لِتُبْغِيه خيراً وليْسَ بفاعل
(Ḥimās came to us driving Ibn Māhā, that you might seek good for him — and he will not do it.)
﴿وَحَال بَيْنَهُمَا المَوْجُ﴾, that is: the water came between Noah's son and the mountain.
His saying: ﴿يٰأَرْضُ ٱبْلَعِي﴾: one says «بَلِعَتْ» and «بَلَعَتْ».

farraa:46-46.t:
His saying: ﴿يٰنُوحُ إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ﴾ whom I [promised] to save. «[Translator's note: the source has a gap here: «الذى و-- أنجيهم».]» Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿إِنَّهُ عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صَالِحٍ﴾ (and the general body of readers follow it). Muḥammad related to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ related to us, saying: Ḥibbān related to me from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, to that effect; he says: your asking Me about that of which you have no knowledge is a deed that is not righteous. And the general body of readers follow it. (al-Farrāʾ related to us,) saying: Abū Isḥāq al-Shaybānī related to me, saying: Abū Rawq related to me from Muḥammad ibn Juḥāda, from his father, from ʿĀʾisha, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ read (إنه عَمِلَ غَيْرَ صالحٍ). (al-Farrāʾ related to us,) saying: Ibn Abī Yaḥyā related to me from a man whom he named — he said: I think he was none other than Thābit al-Bunānī — from Shahr ibn Ḥawshab, from Umm Salama, who said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, how shall I read it? He said: (إنه عملَ غَيْرَ صَالحٍ). «[Translator's note: «الكلمىّ» in the printed text is evidently «الكلبىّ» (al-Kalbī).]»
His saying: ﴿فَلاَ تَسْئَلْنِ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ﴾. It is also read «تسأَلَنىِّ», with the yāʾ retained and the nūn doubled. It is permissible to read it (فَلاَ تَسْأَلَنَّ مَا لَيْسَ) with fatḥa on the nūn, making it fall only on (ما); there is no yāʾ in it in the written text. The readers have disagreed about words ending in yāʾ where it is dropped in the written text: some retain it and some drop it. Of that are (أَكْرَمَنِ), (أهانَنِ) and (فَمَا آتانِ اللّهُ), and it is frequent in the Qur'an.

farraa:48-48.t: His saying: ﴿بِسَلاَمٍ مِّنَّا وَبَركَاتٍ عَلَيْكَ وَعَلَىٰ أُمَمٍ مِّمَّن مَّعَكَ﴾ means the offspring of those with him among the people of felicity. Then He said: (وَأُمَمٌ) of the people of wretchedness (سَنُمَتِّعُهُمْ). Had it been (وَأُمَمًاً سَنُمَتِّعْهُمْ) in the accusative, it would be permissible, with (سَنُمتِّعهم) falling upon them, as He said ﴿فَرِيقاً هَدَى وَفَرِيقاً حَقَ عَلَيْهمُ الضَّلاَلةُ﴾.

farraa:49-49.t:
His saying: ﴿تِلْكَ مِنْ أَنْبَآءِ ٱلْغَيْبِ﴾: (ذَلِكَ) would fit in its place, like His saying ﴿ذَلِكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ القُرَى نَقُصُّهُ عَلَيْكَ﴾. The Arabs do this with the maṣdars of a verb when it is not mentioned, as when you say: "So-and-so has arrived," and the other says: «قد فرحت بها» and «وبه» ("I am glad of it"). Whoever uses the feminine refers to «القَدْمة» (the arrival), and whoever uses the masculine refers to «القدوم». It is like His saying ﴿ثُمَّ تَابُوا مِنْ بَعْدِهَا وآمَنُوا﴾.
His saying: ﴿مَا كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُهَا أَنْتَ وَلاَ قَوْمُكَ﴾. He is saying: the knowledge of Noah and of the nations after him was not part of your knowledge nor your people's knowledge ﴿مِنْ قبْلِ هَذَا﴾, meaning the Qur'an.

farraa:52-52.t: His saying: ﴿يُرْسِلِ ٱلسَّمَآءَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِّدْرَاراً﴾. He is saying: He makes it pour abundantly upon you when there is need of rain, not that it pours night and day. His saying ﴿وَيَزِدْكُمْ قُوَّةً إِلَىٰ قُوَّتِكُمْ﴾: they reported that children had ceased to be born to them for three years. He said (قُوَّةً) because children and wealth are strength.

farraa:54-54.t: His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ ٱعْتَرَاكَ بَعْضُ آلِهَتِنَا بِسُوۤءٍ﴾. They called him a liar, then made him out to be deranged, and claimed that their gods were the ones who had driven him mad because of his finding fault with their gods. Thereupon he said: "I call Allah to witness, and I call you to witness, that I am free of them."

farraa:57-57.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَضُرُّونَهُ شَيْئاً﴾ is nominative because it came after the fāʾ. Had it been jussive, it would be as He said: ﴿مَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللهُ فَلاَ هَادِىَ لَهُ وَيَذرْهُمْ﴾ — that would be correct. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (وَلاَ تَنْقُضُوهُ) in the jussive. The meaning of «لا تضرّوه» is: your destruction, when He destroys you, does not diminish Him in anything.
And (عادٌ) is declined as a triptote (mujrā) throughout the Qur'an; there is no disagreement about it. Its declension may be dropped when it is made the name of the nation of which he was, as the poet said:
أحقّا عبادَ الله جُرْأة مُحْلِقٍ * علىَّ وقد أعييتُ عَادَ وتُبَّعا
(Is it true, O servants of Allah, that Muḥliq dares against me, when I have worn out ʿĀd and Tubbaʿ?)
And al-Kisāʾī heard some of the Arabs say: «إن عادَ وتَبَّعَ أَمَّتان» ("ʿĀd and Tubbaʿ are two nations").

farraa:61-61.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِلَىٰ ثَمُودَ أَخَاهُمْ صَالِحاً﴾. You put «صالحاً», «هوداً» and whatever is of this wording in the accusative by implying (أرسلنا) ("We sent").
The readers have disagreed about (ثَمُود): some of them decline it as a triptote in every case, and some do not in any case.
Muḥammad related to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ related to us, saying: Qays related to me from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad ibn Yazīd al-Nakhaʿī, from his father, that he did not decline (ثمود) as a triptote anywhere in the Qur'an (and Ḥamza read accordingly). Some of them declined (ثمود) as a triptote in the accusative, because it is written with alif throughout the Qur'an except in one place: ﴿وآتَيْنَا ثَمُودَ النَّاقَةَ مُبْصِرَةً﴾. al-Kisāʾī adopted that, declining it as a triptote in the accusative but not in the genitive or the nominative, except in one place: His saying ﴿أَلا إن ثَمُوداً كَفَرُوا رَبَّهُمْ أَلاَ بُعْداً لثمودٍ﴾. They asked him about that, and he said: it was read in the genitive as declined, and it is ugly for the word to occur twice in two places and then differ, so I declined it because of its nearness to it. «[Translator's note: «النَخَمِىّ» in the printed text is evidently «النَخَعِىّ» (al-Nakhaʿī).]»

farraa:63-63.t: His saying: ﴿فَمَا تَزِيدُونَنِي غَيْرَ تَخْسِيرٍ﴾. He is saying: you increase me in nothing but [my declaring] loss for you and [my declaring] error for you; that is, whenever you offer some excuse, it increases you in loss. It is not "nothing but loss for me." It is like your saying to a man: "You increase me in nothing but anger," that is, anger at you.

farraa:68-68.t: His saying: ﴿كَفرُواْ رَبَّهُمْ﴾. It has come in the exegesis: they were ungrateful for the favour of their Lord. The Arabs say: «كفرتك» and «كفرت بك», «شكرتك», «شكرت بك» and «شكرت لك». al-Kisāʾī said: I heard the Arabs say «شكرت بالله», like their saying «كفرت بالله».

farraa:69-69.t:
His saying: ﴿سَلاَماً قَالَ سِلْمُ﴾: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī read it [so], and it is reported from the Prophet ﷺ that he read it thus. In meaning it is «سلام», as they say «حِلّ» and «حَلاَل», «حِرْم» and «حَرَام», because the exegesis has come: they greeted him and he returned [the greeting] to them. So you see that the meaning of «سِلْم» and «سلام» is one, and Allah knows best. One of the Arabs recited to me:
مررنا فقلنا إيه سِلْم فسلَّمت * كما اكتلَّ بالبرق الغمامُ اللوائح
(We passed and said: "Well then — peace!" and she greeted [us], as the gleaming clouds flash with lightning.)
This is evidence that they greeted and she returned it to them. The general body of readers read it (قَالُواْ سَلاَماً قَالَ سَلاَمٌ), the first in the accusative and the second in the nominative. Had both been nominative, or both accusative, it would be correct. Whoever uses the nominative implies (عليكم) ("upon you") even though he does not make it overt, as the poet said:
فقلنا السلامُ فاتَّقت من أميرها * فما كان إلاَّ وَمْؤها بالحواجب
(We said: "Peace!" and she was wary of her guardian, so there was nothing but her signalling with her eyebrows.)
The Arabs say: «التقينا فقلنَا: سَلامٌ سلام» ("we met and said: Peace, peace"). Another argument for the nominative of the second is that the people greeted, and he said, when he did not recognise them: "It is peace, if Allah wills — so who are you?", because he did not recognise them. That is a good interpretation. In this sense it is said: «نحن سِلْم» ("we are at peace"), because greeting does not come from an enemy people.
His saying: ﴿فَمَا لَبِثَ أَن جَاءَ بِعِجْلٍ حَنِيذٍ﴾: «أن» is in the position of the accusative, (لبِث) falling upon it, as though you said: "he was not slow in bringing a calf"; when you dropped the preposition (al-ṣifa), the verb fell upon it. It may also be nominative, making «أن» the agent of «لبث», as though you said: "his bringing a roasted calf was not slow." al-Ḥanīdh is [meat] for which you dig a pit in the ground and then cover it over; it is a well-known practice of the desert people. It is originally «محنوذ», and «حَنِيذ» was said, as «طَبيخ» is said for «المطبوخ» ("cooked") and «قتيل» for «المقتول» ("killed").

farraa:70-70.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلَمَّا رَأَى أَيْدِيَهُمْ لاَ تَصِلُ إِلَيْهِ نَكِرَهُمْ﴾: that is, to the food. That was because it was a custom in their time that when people came to them and were brought food and did not touch it, they thought that they were enemies or thieves. Thereupon he sensed fear within himself, and they saw that in his face and said: "Do not fear." At that his wife laughed; she was standing and he was sitting (and so it is in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: «وامرأته قائِمة وهو قاعد»). [So it is] in order: she laughed, and was given glad tidings after the laughter. She laughed only from joy at the safety, so they followed it for her with the glad tidings of Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob. Some exegetes say: this is put forward and put back [in order]; the meaning is: "We gave her the glad tidings of Isaac, and she laughed after the glad tidings." That is something the speech may bear, and Allah knows best what is correct. As for [the claim that] (فضحِكتْ) means "she menstruated," we have not heard it from a trustworthy person.
His saying (يَعقُوب) is read in the nominative and in the accusative. Ḥamza intended the genitive by it, meaning: (ومن وراء إسحاق بيعقوب). But the genitive is not permissible unless the bāʾ is made overt. Jacob here is the grandson. The accusative in «يعقوب» is like the saying of the poet:
جئنى بمثل بنى بدر لقومهم * أو مثلَ أُسرة منظور بن سَيَّار
أو عامرَ بن طُفَيل فى مُرَكَّبِه * أو حارثا يوم نادى القومُ يا حارِ
(Bring me the like of the Banū Badr for their people, or the like of the family of Manẓūr ibn Sayyār, or ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl in his lineage, or Ḥārith on the day the people called out: "O Ḥār!")
One of the Banū Bāhila recited to me:
لو جيتَ بالخُبز له مُيَسِّرا * والبيضَ مطبوخاً معاً والسُّكَّرا * لم يُرضه ذلك حتى يسكرا *
(If you brought him bread readily, and eggs cooked together with it, and sugar, that would not please him until he got drunk.)
He put [«السكّر»] in the accusative on the assumption of your saying «وجِئتَ بالسكَّر» ("and you brought sugar"); since the verb was not made overt with the wāw, he used the accusative, as when you command a man to pass by his brother and say: «أخاك أخاك» ("your brother, your brother!"), meaning: pass by him.

farraa:72-72.t: His saying: ﴿يَٰوَيْلَتَىٰ أَأَلِدُ وَأَنَاْ عَجُوزٌ وَهَـٰذَا بَعْلِي شَيْخاً﴾. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is (شَيْخٌ). They reported that she was ninety-eight years old, and he (peace be upon him) was a year older than she. And it is said of His saying ﴿رَحْمَةُ اللّهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: «البركات» is felicity.

farraa:74-74.t: His saying: ﴿فَلَمَّا ذَهَبَ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ ٱلرَّوْعُ وَجَآءَتْهُ ٱلْبُشْرَىٰ يُجَادِلُنَا فِي قَوْمِ لُوطٍ﴾ — and He did not say «جادلنا» ("he argued with Us", past). Its like in ordinary speech comes only with a past verb, as when you say: «فلمّا أتانى أتيته» ("when he came to me, I came to him"). But «فلمَّا أتانى أَثِبُ عليه» ("when he came to me I [set about] leaping on him") is permissible, as though he said: "I set about leaping on him." His arguing with them was that when the fear left him he said: "What is your business, O messengers?" And when they told him that they intended the people of Lot, he said: "Will you destroy a people among whom is Lot?" They said: "We know better who is in it."

farraa:75-75.t:
His saying: ﴿أَوَّاهٌ﴾: one who supplicates much. And it is said: he is the one who sighs ("ah!") over sins. If it is from "one who sighs over sins," then it is from «أوِّهْ له», which is a dialect form among the Banū ʿĀmir. Abū al-Jarrāḥ recited to me:
فأوِّهْ من الذكرى إذا ما ذكرتها * ومن بُعد أرض بيننا وسَمَاءِ
(Ah, for the memory whenever I recall her, and for the distance of land and sky between us!)
«أوِّهْ» is on the pattern «فَعِّل»; in the imperfect (yafʿal) he says «يتأَوَّه». It is permissible in speech, for one who says «أوَّهْ» in the shortened form, to say in the «يتفعَّل» pattern «يتأَوَّى», and he does not say it with hāʾ.

farraa:78-78.t: His saying: ﴿هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ بَنَاتِي﴾. Some said: his own daughters. And it is said: the daughters of his people. That is permissible in Arabic, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿النَّبِىُّ أَوْلَى بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ مِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ وَأَزْوَاجُهُ أُمَّهَاتُهُمْ﴾, and in some readings there is (وهو أب لهم) ("and he is a father to them"). So this is of that kind.

farraa:80-81.t:
His saying: ﴿لَوْ أَنَّ لِي بِكُمْ قُوَّةً أَوْ آوِيۤ إِلَىٰ رُكْنٍ شَدِيدٍ﴾. He is saying: to a clan.
His saying: ﴿فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ﴾: our reading is from «أسريت», with fatḥa on the alif and a hamza on it. The reading of the people of Medina is (فاسْرِ بأَهْلِكَ), from «سَريت». His saying: (بِقِطْعٍ): He is saying: in the darkness at the end of the night. His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ ٱمْرَأَتَكَ﴾ is accusative by exception: "so travel by night with your family, except your wife." al-Ḥasan used to put it in the nominative, conjoining it to (أحد), that is: "let none of you look back except your wife." In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh there is no (ولا يلتفت منكم أحد). And His saying: ﴿إِنَّ مَوْعِدَهُمُ ٱلصُّبْحُ أَلَيْسَ ٱلصُّبْحُ بِقَرِيبٍ﴾.
When they came to Lot, they told him that his people would perish the next day in the morning. Lot said to them: "Now! Now!" The angels said: "Is not the morning near?"

farraa:82-82.t: His saying: ﴿مِّن سِجِّيلٍ﴾: it is said: of clay that had been baked until it became like millstones. (مَنْضُودٍ): He is saying: one following another upon them; that is its being "layered" (naḍd).

farraa:83-83.t: His saying: ﴿مُّسَوَّمَةً﴾: they claimed that they were streaked with red, and black on white; that is their «تسويم», that is, their marking. Then He said ﴿مِنَ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ بِبَعِيدٍ﴾. He is saying: from the wrongdoers of your nation, O Muhammad. And it is said: they are not [far] from the wrongdoers, meaning the people of Lot, who were not missed by them. «[Translator's note: the printed text reads «قولم لوط أَلذى يكن تخطِئهم», evidently a corruption of «قوم لوط الذين لم تكن تخطئهم»; translated as so understood.]»

farraa:84-84.t: His saying: ﴿إِنِّيۤ أَرَاكُمْ بِخَيْرٍ﴾. He is saying: your wealth is abundant, so do not diminish the measure while your wealth is abundant. It is said: your prices are cheap. (And it is said:) well-anointed, your complexion good.

farraa:86-86.t: His saying: ﴿بَقِيَّةُ ٱللَّهِ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ﴾. He is saying: what He leaves you of the lawful is better for you. And it is said: «بقيَّة الله خير لكم», that is: watchfulness of Allah is better for you.

farraa:87-87.t:
His saying: ﴿أَصَلَٰوتُكَ تَأْمُرُكَ أَن نَّتْرُكَ﴾. It is also read ﴿أَصَلاَتُكَ تَأْمُرُكَ أَنْ نَتْرُكَ مَا يَعْبُدُ آبَاؤَنَا أَوْ أَنْ نفْعَلَ﴾. Its meaning is: or does it command you that we leave off doing ﴿فِيۤ أَمْوَالِنَا مَا نَشَاءُ﴾; so «أن» is referred back to (نَتْرك).
There is another interpretation in it: you make the command like a prohibition, as though he said: "Does your prayer command you to do this and forbid us to do that?" It is then referred back to the first (أَن), with nothing implied in it, as though you said: "it forbids us to do with our wealth whatever we wish," as you say: «أضرِبُك أَن تُسِيىء» ("I beat you [lest] you do wrong"), as though he said: I forbid you, by beating, from doing wrong. It is also read (أَوْ أَنْ نَفْعلَ فىِ أمْوالِنَا ما تَشاء) and (نَشَاءُ) — both.
His saying: ﴿إِنَّكَ لأَنتَ ٱلْحَلِيمُ ٱلرَّشِيدُ﴾ is mockery of him on their part.

farraa:89-89.t: His saying: ﴿لاَ يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شِقَاقِي﴾. He is saying: let not your enmity towards me drive you [to that] such that it befalls you. It may also be: let it not earn you. His saying ﴿وَمَا قَوْمُ لُوطٍ مِّنكُم بِبَعِيدٍ﴾. He is saying: they perished only yesterday, recently. And it is said: their dwellings are near you («قريبة» and «قريب»). «[Translator's note: the printed text reads «دراهم», evidently for «دارهم» ("their abode").]»

farraa:92-92.t: His saying: ﴿أَرَهْطِيۤ أَعَزُّ عَلَيْكُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَٱتَّخَذْتُمُوهُ وَرَآءَكُمْ ظِهْرِيّاً﴾: you have thrown the command of Allah behind your backs; as you say: you exalt the matter of my clan and neglect to exalt Allah and fear Him.

farraa:93-93.t:
His saying: ﴿مَن يَأْتِيهِ عَذَابٌ يُخْزِيهِ﴾: (مَن) is in the position of the nominative if you make it interrogative; you make it nominative by the pronoun referring back to it. Likewise His saying (وَمَنْ هُوَ كَاذِبٌ). The Arabs brought in (هو) in His saying (وَمَنْ هُوَ كَاذِبٌ) only because they do not say «مَن قائِمٌ» or «مَن قاعد»; their speech is only «من يقوم», «من قامَ» or «من القائِم». Since they do not say it except with a definite noun or with «فَعَل» or «يفعل», they brought in «هو» with «قائم» so that the two together stand in the place of «فَعَل» and «يفعل», because they stand in the place of two [elements]. «مَنْ قائِم» may be allowed in poetry and the like; the poet said:
مَنْ شارب مُرْبِح بالكَأس نادمَنى * لا بالحَصُورِ ولا فيها بسوَّار
(Who is a drinker, generous with the cup, who kept me company — neither stingy nor quarrelsome over it?)
Sometimes the Arabs shrink from following «مَنْ» with an indefinite noun, so they put it in the genitive and say: «مِنْ رجلٍ يتصدَّق», putting it in the genitive on the interpretation: «هَل مِن رجل يتصدّق» ("is there any man who will give charity?"). They have recited this verse to us both with the genitive and the nominative:
مَِن رسولٌٍ إلى الثريّا تأنى * ضِقت ذرعاً بهجرهَا والكتابِ
(Who [or: is there any] messenger to al-Thurayyā [to tell her] that I am at the end of my strength from her estrangement and from the letter?)
If you make «مَن» and «مِن» both in the place of (الذى) ("the one who"), you use the accusative, as in His saying ﴿يَعْلَمُ المُفْسِدَ مِنَ المُصْلِحِ﴾ and His saying ﴿وَلَمَّا يَعْلمِ اللّهُ الذِينَ جَاهَدُوا مِنْكُمْ وَيعْلَمَ الصَّابِرِينَ﴾.

farraa:100-100.t: His saying: ﴿مِنْهَا قَآئِمٌ وَحَصِيدٌ﴾: «الحَصيد» is like harvested crops. And it is said: He mowed them down with the sword as crops are harvested.

farraa:105-105.t:
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يَأْتِ لاَ تَكَلَّمُ﴾ is written without the yāʾ, and it is in the position of the nominative. If you retain the yāʾ in it when continuing the recitation, that is correct; and if you drop it both in pausing and in continuing, that is correct. The readers have read thus. So the one who drops it [entirely] says, when continuing: the yāʾ is quiescent, and every yāʾ or wāw that is quiescent, with what precedes the wāw having ḍamma and what precedes the yāʾ having kasra, the Arabs drop them and make do with the ḍamma in place of the wāw and the kasra in place of the yāʾ. One of them recited to me:
كفّاك كفّ ما تُليق دِرهماً * جُوداً وأخرى تُعطِ بالسيف الدَمَا
(Your two hands: one hand that out of generosity keeps no dirham, and another that gives blood by the sword.)
And whoever continues with the yāʾ and drops it in pausing says: when I continue, it is in the position of the nominative, so I retain it; and when I pause on it, it becomes quiescent, so I drop it — as it is said: «لم يَرْم» and «لم يَقْض». Like it is His saying: ﴿ما كُنَّا نَبْغِ﴾, written with the yāʾ dropped; the proper way in it is to retain the yāʾ when continuing and drop it when pausing. The other way is to drop it in pausing and in continuing; Ḥamza read thus, and it is permissible. «[Translator's note: the printed text reads «فمَر حَذفها», evidently for «فمَن حذفها» ("so the one who drops it").]»

farraa:106-106.t: His saying: ﴿لَهُمْ فِيهَا زَفِيرٌ وَشَهِيقٌ﴾: «الزفير» is the beginning of the braying of a donkey and the like, and «الشهِيق» is from its end.

farraa:107-108.t: His saying: ﴿خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا مَا دَامَتِ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتُ وَٱلأَرْضُ إِلاَّ مَا شَآءَ رَبُّكَ﴾. Someone may ask: what is this exception, when Allah has promised the people of the Fire eternity and the people of the Garden eternity? There are two ways in that. One of them is that you make it an exception He states but does not carry out, as when you say: "By Allah, I will surely beat you, unless I see otherwise," while your resolve is to beat him. Likewise He said ﴿خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا مَا دَامَتِ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتُ وَٱلأَرْضُ إِلاَّ مَا شَآءَ رَبُّكَ﴾ and He does not will it — and Allah knows best. The other view is that when the Arabs except something large along with its like, or with what is larger than it, the meaning of «إلاَّ» and the meaning of the wāw are the same. Of that is His saying ﴿خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا مَا دَامَتِ السَّمَوَاتُ والأَرْضُ﴾ besides what He wills of additional eternity; so «إلاَّ» is put in the place of «سِوَى» ("besides"), and that is sound. It is as though He said: "abiding in it for the duration of the heavens and the earth, besides what He has added for them of eternity and everlastingness." Its like in speech is to say: "You owe me a thousand, except (illā) the two thousand that are on account of So-and-so"; do you not see that in meaning it is: "you owe me [a thousand] besides the two thousand"? This is the dearer of the two interpretations to me, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not break His promise; and He has joined to the exception His saying ﴿عَطَآءً غَيْرَ مَجْذُوذٍ﴾, which shows that the exception, for them, is with eternity uninterrupted for them. «[Translator's note: the printed text reads «مضيان», evidently for «معنيان» ("two meanings").]»

farraa:111-111.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِنَّ كُـلاًّ لَّمَّا لَيُوَفِّيَنَّهُمْ﴾. The readers read (لَمَّا) with doubling and lightened, and «إن» with doubling and lightened. Whoever says ﴿وَإنَّ كُلاَّ لَمَا﴾ makes (ما) a noun for people, as He said ﴿فَانْكِحُوا مَا طَابَ لَكُمْ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ﴾; then he makes the lām in it the answer to «إنّ», and makes the lām in (لَيُوَفِّيَنَّهُمْ) a lām that has entered on the intention of an oath in it, between «ما» and its ṣila (relative clause), as you say: «هذا مَن لَيذهبنَّ» ("this is one who will surely go") and «عندى ما لَغَيْرُهُ خير منه» ("I have something than which something else is surely better"). Like it is ﴿وإنَّ مِنْكُمْ لَمَنْ ليُبَطِّئَن﴾.
As for whoever doubles (لمّا), he — and Allah knows best — meant: «لِمن ما لَيُوَفِّينَّهم»; when three mīms came together, he dropped one, so two remained, and he assimilated it into its companion, as the poet said:
وإنى لَمِمَّا أُصدر الأمرَ وَجْهَهُ * إذا هو اْعيا بالسبيل مصادرُه
(And I am surely of those who bring an affair out by its proper way, when its ways out have proved too hard to find.)
Then it is lightened, as some readers read (وَالبَغْىِ يَعِظُكْمْ), dropping the yāʾ (next to the yāʾ). al-Kisāʾī recited to me:
وأَشمتَّ العُداة بنا فأضحَوا * لدَىَّ تَبَاشَرُونَ بما لِقينَا
(You made the enemies gloat over us, so that in my presence they rejoiced at what we had met.)
Its meaning is (لدىَّ) «يتباشرون»; he dropped [the yāʾ] because of the meeting of the yāʾs. Like it is:
كأنّ مِن آخرهَا إلقادِمِ * مَخْرِمَ نجدٍ فارعَ المخارم
(As if from its rear to the front [of the caravan] were a pass of Najd, tallest of passes.)
He meant «إلى القادم», and dropped the lām next to the lām.
As for whoever makes (لَمَّا) equivalent to «إلاَّ», that is a way we do not know. The Arabs have said: «بالله لَمَّا قمت عنا» and «وإلاَّ قمت عنا» ("by Allah, [I ask nothing] but that you leave us"); but in exception they have not said it, in poetry or otherwise. Do you not see that, were that permissible, you would hear in speech: «ذهب الناسَ لَمّا زيدا» ("the people went, except Zayd")?
As for those who lightened (إن), they put «كلا» in the accusative by (لَيُوفَّينَّهم), and said: it is as though we said: «وإنْ لَيوَفِّينَّهم كُلاَّ». It is a way I do not favour, because with the lām, the verb after it does not fall on something before it. Had you put «كلّ» in the nominative, that would be sound, as it is sound to say: «إنْ زيد لقائم» ("Zayd is indeed standing"), but it is not sound to say «إنْ زيداً لأَضربُ», because its interpretation is like your saying «ما زيداً إلاّ أضرب», and this is an error both with «إلاّ» and with the lām.
al-Zuhrī read (وإنَّ كُلاًّ لَمًّا ليُوَفِّيَنَّهم), with nunation, making «اللمّ» [mean] "intense," as He said ﴿وَتَأْكُلُون التُرَاثَ أَكْلاُ لَمّاً﴾. It is then in the speech like your saying: "and to each, truly, He will surely pay in full," and "and to each, intensely, He will surely pay in full." When the Arabs bring the lām forward to other than its place, they repeat it in its place, as when you say: «إنَّ زيدا لإليك لمحسن» ("Zayd is surely to you surely beneficent"): the position of the lām was on «المحسن», but when it was brought in on «إليك», it was repeated on «المحسن». Like it is the saying of the poet:
ولو أنَّ قومى لم يكونوا أعِزّة * لَبَعْدُ لقد لاقيتُ لا بدّ مَصْرعَا
(Had my people not been mighty, I would surely, after that, have met a fall without fail.)
He brought it in on (بعد), which is not its place. Like it is the saying of Abū al-Jarrāḥ: «إنى لبحمد الله لصالح» ("I am — surely, praise be to Allah — surely well").

farraa:114-114.t: His saying: ﴿زُلَفاً مِّنَ ٱلْلَّيْلِ﴾: with ḍamma on the lām, you make it singular, like «الحُلُم». «الزُلَف» is the plural of «زُلْفة», and «زُلَف» is the reading of the general body of readers; it is an hour of the night. Its meaning is: the two ends of the day and the obligatory night prayer: al-Maghrib and al-ʿIshāʾ; and the dawn prayer; and the two ends of the day: and al-ʿAṣr. «[Translator's note: the source text here is compressed and apparently disordered; translated as written.]»

farraa:116-116.t: His saying: ﴿فَلَوْلاَ كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْقُرُونِ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ أُوْلُواْ بَقِيَّةٍ يَنْهَوْنَ﴾. He is saying: there was none of them like that except a few, that is, these used to forbid [corruption], so they were saved. It is an exception cut off (munqaṭiʿ) from what precedes, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said ﴿إلاَّ قَوْمَ يُونُسَ﴾. Had it been nominative, it would be correct. His saying: ﴿وَٱتَّبَعَ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ مَآ أُتْرِفُواْ فِيهِ﴾. He is saying: they followed in their worldly life the luxury they were accustomed to, and preferred pleasures over the affair of the Hereafter. And it is said: they followed their sins and their evil deeds into the Fire.

farraa:117-117.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ لِيُهْلِكَ ٱلْقُرَىٰ بِظُلْمٍ وَأَهْلُهَا مُصْلِحُونَ﴾.
He is saying: He would not destroy them while they were doing right, so that that would be injustice. And it is said: He would not destroy them while they dealt justly among themselves, even though they were polytheists; and «الظلم» is polytheism.

farraa:118-118.t: His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يَزَالُونَ مُخْتَلِفِينَ﴾. He is saying: (لا يَزَالونَ), meaning the people of falsehood, ﴿إلاَّ مَنْ رَحِمَ رَبُّكَ﴾ — the people of truth. (وَلِذَلِكَ خَلَقَهُمْ): He is saying: for wretchedness and for felicity. And it is said: ﴿ولا يزالونَ مختلفينَ إلاّ من رحم ربُّكَ ولِذَلِكَ خَلَقَهُمْ﴾: for disagreement and for mercy.

farraa:119-120.t:
His saying: ﴿وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ لأَمْلأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ﴾. His saying, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ﴾ became an oath, as you say: «حَلِفى لأضربنَّك» ("my oath: I will surely beat you") and «بدا لى لأضربنّك» ("it occurred to me: I will surely beat you"). Every verb whose interpretation is like the interpretation of «بلغنى» ("it reached me"), «قيل لى» ("it was said to me") and «انتهىَ إلىّ» ("it came to me"), the lām and «أن» are both sound in it. So you say: «قد بدا لى لأضربنّك» and «بدا لى أن أضربك». Had it been «وتَمَّت كلمة ربك أن يملأ جهنم», it would be correct. Likewise ﴿ثُمَّ بَدَالَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ ما رَأَوُا الآياتِ لَيَسْجُنُنَّهُ﴾; had it been «أن يسجنوه», it would be correct.
And He said: ﴿وَجَآءَكَ فِي هَـٰذِهِ ٱلْحَقُّ﴾: in this sūra.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿الر﴾: the discussion of the disjointed letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿa) has preceded at the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqara.
﴿كتاب أحكمت آياته﴾: كتاب is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «هذا كتاب» ("this is a Book"); the clause أحكمت آياته is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿كتاب﴾; and آياته is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
﴿ثم فصلت من لدن حكيم خبير﴾: ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay; فصلت is a past verb built for that whose agent is not named (passive); من is a preposition, and لدن is an adverb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of a genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq) to ﴿فصلت﴾, or to an omitted adjective of كتاب; حكيم is the muḍāf ilayhi (second term of the genitive construct); and خبير is an adjective of حكيم.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿ألا تعبدوا إلا الله﴾: ﴿أن﴾: a maṣdar-forming particle that puts [the verb] in the accusative; ﴿لا﴾ is negative; ﴿تعبدوا﴾ is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن; and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from the maṣdar-forming ﴿أن﴾ and what falls in its scope is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) with an implied lām, i.e. «لئلا تعبدوا» ("so that you not worship"); and the clause ﴿لا تعبدوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the maṣdar-forming ﴿أن﴾, with no grammatical position. Or ﴿أن﴾ is explicative (tafsīriyya), because "setting out in detail" (al-tafṣīl) carries the meaning of speech without its letters, as if it were said: He set out in detail and said: «لا تعبدوا إلا الله» ("worship none but Allah"); ﴿لا﴾ is then prohibitive, ﴿تعبدوا﴾ is a jussive (majzūm) imperfect verb, and the clause ﴿لا تعبدوا﴾ is explicative with no grammatical position. إلا: a particle of restriction (adāt ḥaṣr), and the Divine Name is the object of تعبدوا.
﴿إنني لكم منه نذير وبشير﴾: ﴿إن﴾ is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); the yāʾ is its noun (ism), and the nūn is for protection (nūn al-wiqāya); ﴿لكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نذير وبشير﴾; ﴿منه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); نذير is the khabar of إنّ; and بشير is conjoined to نذير.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿وأن استغفروا ربكم ثم توبوا إليه﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿أن استغفروا﴾ is conjoined to ﴿ألا تعبدوا﴾; ربكم is the object of استغفروا; ﴿ثم﴾ is a conjunction; and توبوا is conjoined to ﴿استغفروا﴾. Or ﴿وأن استغفروا﴾ and what follows it is speech begun anew, cut off from what precedes it, on the tongue of the Prophet ﷺ, as an urging (ighrāʾ) from him to devote worship exclusively to Allah; this is indicated by His saying: ﴿إنني لكم منه نذير وبشير﴾.
﴿يمتعكم متاعا حسنا إلى أجل مسمى﴾: يمتعكم is a jussive imperfect verb, because it is the answer to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab), which is His saying ﴿وأن استغفروا ربكم﴾; the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿متاعًا﴾ stands as deputy for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar); حسنًا is an adjective; إلى أجل is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يمتعكم﴾; and مسمى is an adjective of ﴿أجل﴾.
﴿ويؤت كل ذي فضل فضله﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; يؤت is conjoined to يمتعكم and is jussive like it, the sign of its jussive being the deletion of the weak letter; the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو), i.e. Allah; ﴿كل﴾ is the first direct object; ذي فضل is the muḍāf ilayhi; and فضله is the second direct object.
﴿وإن تولوا فإني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم كبير﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional; تولوا is a jussive imperfect verb because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the wāw is the agent; the fāʾ is linking (rābiṭa); إنّ is an abrogating particle, and the yāʾ is its noun; the clause أخاف عليكم is the khabar of إنّ; the clause ﴿فإني أخاف عليكم﴾ is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); عذاب is the direct object; يوم is the muḍāf ilayhi; and كبير is an adjective of ﴿يوم﴾.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t: ﴿إلى الله مرجعكم وهو على كل شيء قدير﴾: إلى الله is a fronted khabar, and مرجعكم is a postponed mubtadaʾ; ﴿هو﴾ is a mubtadaʾ; على كل شيء is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿قدير﴾; and قدير is the khabar of ﴿هو﴾.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿ألا إنهم يثنون صدورهم ليستخفوا منه﴾: ألا is a particle of opening (istiftāḥ) and drawing attention (tanbīh); إنّ is an abrogating particle, and the hāʾ is its noun; the clause يثنون صدورهم is its khabar; the lām is for causation (taʿlīl); يستخفوا is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām, and the interpreted maṣdar formed from the implied أن and the verb is genitive by the lām, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to ﴿يثنون﴾.
﴿ألا حين يستغشون ثيابهم يعلم ما يسرون وما يعلنون﴾: ألا is an emphasis of the drawing of attention; حين is an adverb, and what governs it is implied, namely يستخفون; or it is an adverb of يعلم, i.e. does He not know their secret and their open [deeds] when they do such-and-such; the clause يستغشون is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it; ثيابهم is accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ); يعلم is an imperfect verb, and its agent is "he" (هو), Allah; ما is the direct object; the clause يسرون is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; and ما يعلنون is conjoined to it.
﴿إنه عليم بذات الصدور﴾: إنّ is an abrogating particle, and the hāʾ is its noun; عليم is its khabar; and بذات الصدور is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿عليم﴾.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿وما من دابة في الأرض إلا على الله رزقها﴾: the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa) with no grammatical position; ما is negative; من is an extra (ṣila) particle; دابة is nominative (marfūʿ) in position and genitive by من in wording; إلا is a particle of restriction; على الله is a fronted khabar, and رزقها is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and the nominal clause is the khabar of دابة.
﴿ويعلم مستقرها ومستودعها﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; يعلم is an imperfect verb, and its agent is "he" (هو); مستقرها is the object of يعلم; and مستودعها is conjoined to مستقرها.
﴿كل في كتاب مبين﴾: كل is the mubtadaʾ; في كتاب is the khabar; and مبين is an adjective.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿وهو الذي خلق السماوات والأرض في ستة أيام﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿هو﴾ is the mubtadaʾ, and الذي is the khabar; the clause خلق السماوات والأرض is the ṣila of الذي, with no grammatical position; and في ستة أيام is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to خلق.
﴿وكان عرشه على الماء﴾: كان is a defective (nāqiṣ), abrogating past verb; عرشه is its noun; and ﴿على الماء﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to its omitted khabar.
﴿ليبلوكم أيكم أحسن عملا﴾: the lām is for causation; يبلوكم is an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām of causation, and the genitive-governing lām of causation together with what it governs is attached to خلق; أيكم is the mubtadaʾ, and أحسن is the khabar; عملًا is a tamyīz (specification); and the clause is in the position of an accusative as governed by يبلوكم, which has been suspended (ʿulliqa) from it by the interrogative أيّ.
﴿ولئن قلت إنكم مبعوثون من بعد الموت﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; the lām prepares for an oath (mūṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam); إن is a conditional particle that makes [the verb] jussive; ﴿قلت﴾ is a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis; إنّ is an abrogating particle, and the kāf is its noun; مبعوثون is its khabar; and ﴿من بعد الموت﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿مبعوثون﴾.
﴿ليقولن الذين كفروا إن هذا إلا سحر مبين﴾: the lām is [that of] the answer to the oath, and the answer of the conditional [jazāʾ] is dispensed with by the answer to the oath; يقولن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because it is attached to the nūn of emphasis, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath; إن is negative; هذا is the mubtadaʾ; إلا is a particle of restriction; سحر is the khabar; and مبين is an adjective.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿ولئن أخرنا عنهم العذاب إلى أمة معدودة﴾: ﴿ولئن﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and the lām prepares for an oath; عنهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أخرنا﴾; العذاب is the direct object; إلى أمة is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أخرنا﴾; and معدودة is an adjective of أمة.
﴿ليقولن ما يحبسه﴾: the lām is [that of] the answer to the oath; يقولن is a nominative imperfect verb, because it is separated from the nūn of emphasis by a separator, namely the wāw of the plural, which has been deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; ما is an interrogative noun, the mubtadaʾ; the clause يحبسه is the khabar; and the interrogation is for disapproval (inkār).
﴿ألا يوم يأتيهم ليس مصروفا عنهم﴾: ألا is a particle of interrogation and drawing attention [Translator's note: so in the source, «أداة استفهام وتنبيه»; elsewhere the author calls ألا a particle of opening (istiftāḥ) and drawing attention]; يوم يأتيهم is accusative as an adverb (ʿalā al-ẓarf), and it is governed by the khabar of ليس; its noun is latent, referring back to the punishment; مصروفًا is the khabar of ليس; and عنهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿مصروفًا﴾.
﴿وحاق بهم ما كانوا به يستهزئون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; the clause حاق is conjoined to the clause of ﴿ليس﴾, so it falls within the scope of ﴿ألا﴾; ﴿بهم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿حاق﴾; ما is the agent of حاق; the clause كانوا is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; the wāw is the noun of كان; به is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يستهزئون﴾; and the clause يستهزئون is the khabar of كان.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿ولئن أذقنا الإنسان منا رحمة﴾: ﴿ولئن﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and the lām prepares for an oath; أذقنا is a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis, and نا is the agent; الإنسان is the direct object; منا is a ḥāl; and رحمة is the second direct object.
﴿ثم نزعناها منه إنه ليئوس كفور﴾: ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay; نزعنا[ها] is a verb, its agent and its direct object; منه is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نزعناها﴾; إنّ is an abrogating particle, and the hāʾ is its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); يئوس is the khabar of إنّ; and كفور is a second khabar of ﴿إن﴾.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿ولئن أذقناه نعماء بعد ضراء مسته﴾: ﴿ولئن﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and the lām prepares for an oath; أذقنا is a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis, and نا is the agent; the pronoun is the first direct object; نعماء is the second direct object; بعد is an adverb attached to an omitted adjective of نعماء; ضراء is the muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause مسته is an adjective.
﴿ليقولن ذهب السيئات عني﴾: the lām is [that of] the answer to the oath, and the apodosis of the condition is omitted because the answer to the oath indicates it; يقولن is an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa; the clause ذهب السيئات is what is said (maqūl al-qawl); and ﴿عني﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ذهب﴾.
﴿إنه لفرح فخور﴾: إنّ is an abrogating particle, and the hāʾ is its noun; the lām is the shifted lām; فرح is the first khabar, and فخور is a second khabar of ﴿إن﴾.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿إلا الذين صبروا وعملوا الصالحات﴾: إلا is a particle of exception; الذين is excepted (mustathnā) from الإنسان, in the position of an accusative, because the lām in it is generic, so the exception is connected (muttaṣil); or the exception is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), and الذين is likewise excepted, in the position of an accusative; the clause صبروا is the ṣila of الذين, with no grammatical position; and عملوا الصالحات is conjoined.
﴿أولئك لهم مغفرة وأجر كبير﴾: أولئك is the mubtadaʾ; لهم is a fronted khabar, and مغفرة is a postponed mubtadaʾ; and the nominal clause is the khabar of أولئك.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿فلعلك تارك بعض ما يوحى إليك وضائق به صدرك﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive; لعل is a particle of hope (tarajjī) that puts [its noun] in the accusative, and the kāf is its noun; تارك is its khabar; بعض is the direct object of تارك; ﴿ما﴾ is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi; the clause يوحى is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; إليك is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ضائق﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; إليك presumably belongs with يوحى, while it is به that is attached to ضائق]; صدرك is the agent of ضائق; or ضائق is a fronted khabar and صدرك a postponed mubtadaʾ, the clause being a second khabar of ﴿لعلك﴾.
﴿أن يقولوا لولا أنزل عليه كنز أو جاء معه ملك﴾: أن together with what falls in its scope is a maṣdar in the position of an accusative as an object of purpose (mafʿūl min ajlihi), i.e. for fear of their saying; or it is a badal (substitute) for the hāʾ in His saying ﴿وضائق به صدرك﴾; لولا is for urging (taḥḍīḍiyya); أنزل is a past verb built for that whose agent is not named; عليه is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to it; كنز is the deputy agent; ﴿أو﴾ is a conjunction; جاء is a past verb; ﴿معه﴾ is an adverb attached to ﴿جاء﴾; ملك is the agent; and the clause ﴿فلعلك تارك بعض...﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿إنما أنت نذير والله على كل شيء وكيل﴾: إنما is [إنّ] restrained [from governing] by the restraining [ما] (kāffa wa-makfūfa); أنت is the mubtadaʾ, and نذير is its khabar; ﴿الله﴾ is a mubtadaʾ; ﴿على كل شيء﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿وكيل﴾; and وكيل is the khabar of ﴿الله﴾.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿أم يقولون افتراه﴾: أم is a disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) conjunction, so it has the meaning of بل together with the interrogative hamza, the implied form being: «بل أيقولون افتراه» ("rather, do they say he invented it?"), the hamza being for disapproving interrogation (al-istifhām al-inkārī); or ﴿أم﴾ is connected (muttaṣila), and in that case a clause must be implied so that the balance [between the two alternatives] is correct, the implied form being: «أيقرون به أم يقولون: افتراه؟» ("do they acknowledge it, or do they say: he invented it?"); the clause افتراه is what is said; and ﴿يقولون﴾ is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn.
﴿قل فأتوا بعشر سور مثله مفتريات﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); ائتوا is an imperative verb and its agent; بعشر is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to it; سورة is the muḍāf ilayhi [Translator's note: so in the source, «وسورة»; the Quranic word is سور]; and مثله is an adjective.
﴿وادعوا من استطعتم من دون الله إن كنتم صادقين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ادعوا is conjoined to ﴿فائتوا﴾, and the wāw is the agent; مَن is the direct object; the clause استطعتم is the ṣila of ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position; ﴿من دون الله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl; إن is conditional; ﴿كنتم﴾ is a defective, abrogating past verb, and the tāʾ is its noun, and it is the protasis; صادقين is the khabar of كنتم; and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. then bring and call.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿فإلم يستجيبوا لكم فاعلموا أنما أنزل بعلم الله﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; إن is conditional; لم is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and jussive; يستجيبوا is jussive by ﴿لم﴾, and it is the protasis; the wāw is the agent, and the pronoun refers back to ﴿من استطعتم﴾; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يستجيبوا﴾; the fāʾ is linking; اعلموا is an imperative verb and its agent; أنما is [أنّ] restrained by the restraining [ما] (kāffa makfūfa), which together with what it governs stands in place of the two objects of اعلموا; أنزل is a past verb built for that whose agent is not named; and بعلم الله is a ḥāl, i.e. bound up with the knowledge of Allah, so the bāʾ is for accompaniment (mulābasa).
﴿وأن﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; أن is lightened from the heavy [أنّ] (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla), and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), omitted. ﴿لا﴾: the lā of generic negation.
﴿إله﴾: the noun of لا, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of an accusative.
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction.
﴿هو﴾: a badal for the position of لا together with its noun, because its position is nominative as mubtadaʾ; or a badal for the pronoun latent in the omitted khabar. The clause ﴿لا إله إلا هو﴾ is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of أن.
﴿فهل أنتم مسلمون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; هل is an interrogative particle; أنتم is the mubtadaʾ; and مسلمون is the khabar.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t: ﴿من كان يريد الحياة الدنيا وزينتها نوف إليهم أعمالهم فيها وهم فيها لا يبخسون﴾: من is a conditional noun that makes [the verb] jussive, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; the noun of كان is a latent pronoun referring back to مَن; the clause يريد الحياة الدنيا is the khabar of كان; كان is the protasis, jussive in position; زينتها is conjoined to الحياة; نوف is the apodosis, jussive by the deletion of the weak letter; إليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نوف﴾; أعمالهم is the direct object; فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl; ﴿وهم﴾: the wāw is for the ḥāl (ḥāliyya), and هم is the mubtadaʾ; فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يبخسون﴾; and the clause لا يبخسون is the khabar of هم.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿أولئك الذين ليس لهم في الآخرة إلا النار﴾: the demonstrative is the mubtadaʾ, and الذين is its khabar; the clause of ﴿ليس﴾ is the ṣila of الذين, with no grammatical position; ﴿لهم﴾ is the fronted khabar of ﴿ليس﴾; في الآخرة is a ḥāl; إلا is a particle of restriction; and النار is the postponed noun of ﴿ليس﴾.
﴿وحبط ما صنعوا فيها وباطل ما كانوا يعملون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; حبط is a past verb, and ﴿ما﴾ is its agent; the clause صنعوا is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; or ما is maṣdar-forming, and together with what it governs it is interpreted as a maṣdar that is the agent of حبط; فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿صنعوا﴾ or to ﴿حبط﴾; ﴿وباطل﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and باطل is a fronted khabar; ما is a relative noun, the postponed mubtadaʾ; or ما is maṣdar-forming, and together with what it governs it is interpreted as a maṣdar that is the postponed mubtadaʾ; ﴿وكانوا﴾ is a defective, abrogating past verb, the wāw is its noun, and the clause يعملون is its khabar.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿أفمن كان على بينة من ربه﴾: the hamza is for interrogation seeking affirmation (al-istifhām al-taqrīrī); the fāʾ is resumptive; من is a relative [noun], the mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being: «كغيره» ("like someone else"), or: «كمن ليس كذلك» ("like one who is not so"); the answer to the interrogation is also omitted, its implied form being: «لا يستويان» ("the two are not equal"); كان is a defective past verb, and its noun is latent, referring back to ﴿مَن﴾; ﴿على بينة﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to its omitted khabar; ﴿من ربه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of ﴿بينة﴾; and the clause ﴿أفمن كان...﴾ is resumptive with no grammatical position.
﴿ويتلوه شاهد منه﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; يتلوه شاهد is an imperfect verb, a direct object and an agent; and منه is an adjective of ﴿شاهد﴾.
﴿ومن قبله كتاب موسى إماما ورحمة﴾: the wāw is likewise a conjunction; ﴿من قبله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl of ﴿كتاب موسى﴾, which is conjoined to ﴿شاهد﴾ as a conjoining of single words; or ﴿من قبله﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted khabar, and كتاب موسى is a postponed mubtadaʾ; ﴿إمامًا﴾ is a ḥāl of ﴿كتاب موسى﴾; and رحمة is conjoined to ﴿إمامًا﴾.
﴿أولئك يؤمنون به﴾: أولئك is the mubtadaʾ, and the clause يؤمنون به is the khabar.
﴿ومن يكفر به من الأحزاب فالنار موعده﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; من is conditional, the mubtadaʾ; يكفر is the protasis; ﴿به﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يكفر﴾; ﴿من الأحزاب﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl; the fāʾ is linking; النار is the mubtadaʾ, and موعده is the khabar; and the nominal clause is the apodosis.
﴿فلا تك في مرية منه﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa; لا is prohibitive; ﴿تك﴾ is a jussive imperfect verb, the sign of its jussive being the sukūn implied on the nūn that has been deleted for lightening; the noun of ﴿تك﴾ is latent, its implied form being "you" (أنت); ﴿في مرية﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar; and ﴿منه﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective of ﴿مرية﴾.
﴿إنه الحق من ربك ولكن أكثر الناس لا يؤمنون﴾: إنّ is an abrogating particle, and the hāʾ is its noun; الحق is its khabar; من ربك is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl; the wāw is for the ḥāl; لكنّ is an abrogating particle, and أكثر is its noun; الناس is the muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause لا يؤمنون is the khabar of لكنّ.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿ومن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and the clause after it is resumptive with no grammatical position; مَن is interrogative, the mubtadaʾ [Translator's note: the source does not parse أظلم, which would be the khabar]; ممن is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أظلم﴾; the clause افترى is the ṣila of ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position; على الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿افترى﴾; ﴿كذبا﴾ is the direct object of the verb افترى, i.e. he fabricated and contrived a lie; or an object of purpose, i.e. he fabricated for the sake of lying; or a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl, i.e. he fabricated while being a liar, and it is an emphatic ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida).
﴿أولئك يعرضون على ربهم﴾: أولئك is the mubtadaʾ; the clause يعرضون is its khabar, and the wāw is the deputy agent; and على ربهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يعرضون﴾.
﴿ويقول الأشهاد هؤلاء الذين كذبوا على ربهم ألا لعنة الله على الظالمين﴾: ﴿ويقول﴾ is conjoined to ﴿يعرضون﴾; الأشهاد is the agent; هؤلاء is the mubtadaʾ, and الذين is its khabar; the clause كذبوا على ربهم is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position; ألا is a particle of drawing attention; لعنة الله is the mubtadaʾ; and على الظالمين is the khabar.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿الذين يصدون عن سبيل الله ويبغونها عوجا﴾: الذين is a badal of الظالمين; the clause يصدون is the ṣila of الذين, with no grammatical position; عن سبيل الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يصدون﴾; يبغونها is conjoined to يصدون, and it is a verb, its agent and its object; and عوجًا is a ḥāl, i.e. crooked.
﴿وهم بالآخرة هم كافرون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿هم﴾ is the mubtadaʾ; بالآخرة is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿كافرون﴾; the second ﴿هم﴾ is an emphasis (taʾkīd) of the first ﴿هم﴾; and كافرون is the khabar of the first ﴿هم﴾.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿أولئك لم يكونوا معجزين في الأرض﴾: أولئك is the mubtadaʾ; the clause لم يكونوا is the khabar; معجزين is the khabar of يكونوا; and في الأرض is a ḥāl.
﴿وما كان لهم من دون الله من أولياء﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ما is negative; كان is a defective past verb; لهم is the fronted khabar of كان; من دون الله is a ḥāl; من is an extra (ṣila) particle; and أولياء is the noun of كان in position.
﴿يضاعف لهم العذاب ما كانوا يستطيعون السمع وما كانوا يبصرون﴾: يضاعف is an imperfect verb built for that whose agent is not named; لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to it; العذاب is the deputy agent; and the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position; ما is negative; كانوا: a defective, abrogating past verb, and the wāw is its noun; the clause يستطيعون السمع is the khabar of كان, and السمع is the direct object; and the clause وما كانوا يبصرون is conjoined to ما كانوا يستطيعون السمع.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t: ﴿أولئك الذين خسروا أنفسهم وضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون﴾: أولئك is the mubtadaʾ, and الذين is the khabar; the clause خسروا أنفسهم is the ṣila of الذين, with no grammatical position; ضل عنهم is conjoined; ﴿ما﴾ is the agent of ﴿ضل﴾; and the clause ﴿كانوا يفترون﴾ is the ṣila of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t: ﴿لا جرم أنهم في الآخرة هم الأخسرون﴾: لا is negative, and جرم is a past verb; ﴿أنهم﴾: أنّ together with what falls in its scope is in the position of a nominative as the agent of جرم; في الآخرة is a ḥāl; ﴿هم﴾ is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), or a mubtadaʾ; and الأخسرون is the khabar of أنّ, or the khabar of ﴿هم﴾, the clause [then] being the khabar of أنّ.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات وأخبتوا إلى ربهم﴾: إنّ is an abrogating particle, and الذين is its noun; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila of الذين, with no grammatical position; the clause عملوا الصالحات is conjoined to آمنوا, and likewise the clause ﴿وأخبتوا إلى ربهم﴾.
﴿أولئك أصحاب الجنة هم فيها خالدون﴾: أولئك is the mubtadaʾ, and أصحاب الجنة is the khabar; هم is a mubtadaʾ; فيها is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿خالدون﴾; خالدون is the khabar of ﴿هم﴾; the clause أولئك أصحاب الجنة is the khabar of إنّ; and the clause هم فيها خالدون is a second khabar of ﴿إن﴾.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿مثل الفريقين كالأعمى والأصم والبصير والسميع﴾: مثل is the mubtadaʾ, and الفريقين is the muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿كالأعمى﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (mithl), indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of a nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and الأعمى is the muḍāf ilayhi; الأصم is conjoined to الأعمى, a conjoining of an attribute to an attribute, the two being attributes of one person; ﴿والبصير والسميع﴾ is conjoined to ﴿الأعمى والأصم﴾, and البصير and السميع are two attributes of another person, i.e. like one who combines blindness and deafness and one who combines sight and hearing.
﴿هل يستويان مثلا أفلا تذكرون﴾: هل is an interrogative whose meaning is negation; يستويان is an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; مثلًا is a tamyīz converted from the agent, the original being: «هل يستوي مثلهم» ("is their likeness equal?"); ﴿أفلا تذكرون﴾: the interrogation is for disapproval and rebuke.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t: ﴿ولقد أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه إني لكم نذير مبين﴾: a resumptive clause with no grammatical position; the lām occurs in the answer to an implied oath, and قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); أرسلنا is a verb and its agent; نوحًا is the direct object; إلى قومه is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أرسلنا﴾; ﴿إني﴾: إنّ is an abrogating particle, and the yāʾ is its noun; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نذير﴾; نذير is the khabar of إنّ; and مبين is its adjective.

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
﴿أن لا تعبدوا إلا الله﴾: أن is explicative; لا is prohibitive; تعبدوا is an imperfect verb made jussive by ﴿لا﴾, and the wāw is the agent; إلا is a particle of restriction; and the Divine Name is the direct object. The clause ﴿لا تعبدوا...﴾ is explicative, with no grammatical position.
﴿إني أخاف عليكم عذاب يوم أليم﴾: إنّ is an abrogating particle, and the yāʾ is its noun; the clause أخاف is its khabar; عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أخاف﴾; عذاب يوم is the object of أخاف; and أليم is an adjective of ﴿يوم﴾.

muyesser-irab:27-27.t:
﴿فقال الملأ الذين كفروا من قومه﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; قال الملأ is a verb and its agent; الذين is an adjective of الملأ; the clause كفروا is the ṣila of الذين, with no grammatical position; and من قومه is a ḥāl.
﴿ما نراك إلا بشرا مثلنا وما نراك اتبعك إلا الذين هم أراذلنا بادي الرأي﴾: the clause is what is said; ما is negative; نراك is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object; إلا is a particle of restriction; the seeing may be mental (qalbiyya) or visual (baṣariyya), so ﴿بشرًا﴾ is a second direct object on the first [view] and a ḥāl on the second; مثلنا is an adjective; the [second] ما نراك is conjoined to the first ما نراك, and it too may be mental or visual, so the clause اتبعك is either a second direct object or a ḥāl; إلا is a particle of restriction; الذين is the agent of اتبعك; هم أراذلنا is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the clause is the ṣila of الذين, with no grammatical position; and بادي الرأي is accusative as an adverb (ʿalā al-ẓarfiyya).
﴿وما نرى لكم علينا من فضل بل نظنكم كاذبين﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ما نرى is conjoined to what precedes; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نرى﴾; علينا is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿فضل﴾; من is an extra (ṣila) particle; فضل is genitive in wording and a direct object, accusative in position; بل is a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction; نظنكم is conjoined to ﴿ما نرى﴾; the kāf is the first direct object; and كاذبين is the second direct object.

muyesser-irab:28-28.t:
﴿قال يا قوم أرأيتم إن كنت على بينة من ربي وآتاني رحمة من عنده﴾: the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position; يا قوم is a vocative (munādā) put in construct with the yāʾ of the first person, which has been deleted; ﴿وأرأيتم﴾: the hamza is for interrogation; رأى is a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, and the tāʾ is the agent. Here the verb أرى requires the word البينة as a direct object, while ﴿كنت﴾ requires البينة in the genitive by ﴿على﴾; so the second was made to govern, and [a pronoun] was implied in the first, the implied form being: «أرأيتم البينة من ربي إن كنت عليها أنلزمكموها» ("have you considered the clear proof from my Lord, if I am upon it — shall we compel you to it?"); the first object was then omitted, and the interrogative clause is the second object; the apodosis is omitted because it is indicated. إن is conditional; كنت is the protasis, and the tāʾ is its noun; على بينة is the khabar of كنت; من ربي is an adjective; ﴿وآتاني﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and ﴿آتاني﴾ is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; رحمة is the second direct object; and من عنده is an adjective of رحمة.
﴿فعميت عليكم أنلزمكموها وأنتم لها كارهون﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; عميت is a past verb built for that whose agent is not named, and the deputy agent is latent, its implied form being "she/it" (هي); عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿عميت﴾; أنلزمكموها: the hamza is for interrogation, and the agent is latent, its implied form being "we" (نحن); the kāf is the first object, and ﴿ها﴾ is the second object; the mīm is the sign of the masculine plural, and the wāw is for prolonging the ḍamma on the mīm and is not a pronoun; ﴿وأنتم﴾: the wāw is for the ḥāl; أنتم is the mubtadaʾ; لها is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿كارهون﴾; كارهون is the khabar; and the clause is a ḥāl.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t:
﴿ويا قوم لا أسألكم عليه مالا﴾: conjoined to what precedes; لا is negative; أسألكم is a verb, a latent agent and a direct object; عليه is a ḥāl; and ﴿مالًا﴾ is the second direct object.
﴿إن أجري إلا على الله﴾: إن is negative; أجري is the mubtadaʾ, and the yāʾ of the first person is the muḍāf ilayhi; إلا is a particle of restriction; and على الله is the khabar.
﴿وما أنا بطارد الذين آمنوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿ما﴾ is the Ḥijāzī negative [ما] which operates like ليس; ﴿أنا﴾ is the noun of ما; ﴿بطارد﴾: the bāʾ is an extra (ṣila) preposition, and ﴿طارد﴾ is the khabar of the Ḥijāzī ﴿ما﴾, accusative in position and genitive by the bāʾ in wording; ﴿الذين﴾ is the muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause ﴿آمنوا﴾ is the ṣila of الذين, with no grammatical position.
﴿إنهم ملاقو ربهم ولكني أراكم قوما تجهلون﴾: إنّ is an abrogating particle, and the hāʾ is its noun; ﴿ملاقو﴾ is its khabar, and ربهم is the muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿ولكني﴾: the wāw is for the ḥāl or a conjunction; لكنّ is an abrogating particle, and the yāʾ is its noun; the clause أراكم is its khabar; the kāf is the first object of أراكم; قومًا is the second direct object; and the clause تجهلون is an adjective.
