His saying: ﴿وَلِذَلِكَ خَلَقَهُمْ﴾, that is: He created them for felicity and wretchedness, so their differing in religion leads them to felicity or to wretchedness. It has also been said: ”وَلِذَلِكَ خَلَقَهُمْ“ means: for His mercy He created them, because of His saying: ﴿إلا مَن رَحِمَ رَبُّكَ﴾. The first view is what [the context] indicates.
﴿وَتَمَّتْ كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ لأمْلأنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنَ الجِنَّةِ والنّاسِ أجْمَعِينَ﴾: ”لَأمْلَأنَّ“ has the wording of an oath, that is: "So His saying was fulfilled: I will surely fill Hell".

zajjaj:120-120.t:
﴿وَكُلا نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ مِن أنْباءِ الرُّسُلِ ما نُثَبِّتُ بِهِ فُؤادَكَ﴾: ”كُلًّا“ is accusative (manṣūb) by ”نَقُصُّ“; the meaning is: "And all that is needed of the tidings of the messengers We relate to you". And ”ما“ is accusative, a badal (substitute) for ”كُلًّا“; the meaning is: "We relate to you that by which We make your heart firm". The meaning of making the heart (fuʾād) firm is calming the heart; here it is not because of doubt, but rather the more abundant the proof and the evidence, the firmer the heart, as Ibrāhīm said: ﴿وَلَكِنْ لِيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِي﴾ [al-Baqara: 260].
﴿وَجاءَكَ في هَذِهِ الحَقُّ ومَوْعِظَةٌ وذِكْرى لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: it may be "and there has come to you in this sūra", because it contains the stories of the prophets, admonitions, and mention of what is in Paradise and the Fire. And it may be that His saying ﴿وَجاءَكَ في هَذِهِ الحَقُّ﴾ means: in My mentioning these verses which I mentioned before this place, that is: the truth has come to you in that creation will be recompensed with their shares, in His saying: ﴿وَإنّا لَمُوَفُّوهم نَصِيبَهُمْ﴾ [Hūd: 109], and in His saying: ﴿وَإنَّ كُلا لَمّا لَيُوَفِّيَنَّهُمْ﴾ [Hūd: 111].
The truth has indeed come to him in the whole Qur'an, but He mentioned it here for emphasis (tawkīd). It does not follow, when it is said: "The truth has come to you in this", that the truth has not come to you except in this; rather, some truth is more emphatic than other truth in its manifestness to us and its hiddenness from us, not in itself. When you say: "So-and-so is in the truth (fī al-ḥaqq)", meaning that he is giving up his soul [i.e. dying], he is not, in any state other than that, in falsehood; rather, the mention of "the truth" here suffices in place of mentioning death, because of its gravity, and because at it he arrives at the truth.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat Hūd
﷽
His saying: ﴿الر كِتابٌ أُحْكِمَتْ آياتُهُ﴾ — ”كِتابٌ“ is nominative by the implied [mubtadaʾ (subject)] ”هَذا كِتابٌ“ (this is a Book). Some said: ”كِتابٌ“ is the khabar (predicate) of ”الـر“; this is an error, because His saying ﴿كِتابٌ أُحْكِمَتْ آياتُهُ ثُمَّ فُصِّلَتْ﴾ is not ”الـر“ by itself.
In the tafsīr: its verses were made firm (uḥkimat) with command and prohibition, the lawful and the unlawful, ﴿ثُمَّ فُصِّلَتْ﴾ (then made distinct) with the promise and the threat. The meaning — and Allah knows best — is that its verses were made firm and made distinct with all that is needed of guidance to the Oneness [of Allah], the affirmation of the prophethood of the prophets — peace be upon them — and the establishment of the laws. The proof of that is His saying: ﴿ما فَرَّطْنا في الكِتابِ مِن شَيْءٍ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 38],
and His saying: ﴿وَتَفْصِيلَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ [Yūsuf: 111]. This is also shown by His saying: ﴿ألا تَعْبُدُوا إلا اللَّهَ إنَّنِي لَكم مِنهُ نَذِيرٌ وبَشِيرٌ﴾ [Hūd: 2]. The meaning is: "Its verses were made firm, then made distinct, from One Wise, All-Aware",
i.e. from One Wise, All-Aware, [to the effect] ”ألّا تَعْبُدُوا إلّا اللَّهَ“ (that you worship none but Allah). The position of ”أنْ“ is accusative (naṣb) in every case.
His saying: ﴿إنَّنِي﴾ [Hūd: 2] is the object of an implied (muqaddar) saying, i.e. "Say to them, O Muhammad: ﴿إنَّنِي لَكم مِنهُ﴾ [Hūd: 2]", i.e. from Allah's side, ﴿نَذِيرٌ﴾ [Hūd: 2], i.e. one who warns of His punishment whoever disbelieves, ﴿وَبَشِيرٌ﴾ [Hūd: 2] with Paradise, for whoever believes.

zajjaj:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿إلا الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ﴾ is an exception not from the first [category] (disjunctive exception). The meaning: "But those who are patient and do righteous deeds — for them is forgiveness and a great reward."

zajjaj:12-12.t: His saying: ﴿فَلَعَلَّكَ تارِكٌ بَعْضَ ما يُوحى إلَيْكَ وضائِقٌ بِهِ صَدْرُكَ أنْ يَقُولُوا لَوْلا أُنْـزِلَ عَلَيْهِ كَنْـزٌ﴾ — it is related that the polytheists said to the Prophet ﷺ: "If you stopped finding fault with us and reviling our gods, we would sit with you." The meaning of ”أنْ يَقُولُوا لَوْلا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْهِ كَنْزٌ“ is: ”كَراهَةَ أنْ يَقُولُوا ...“ (out of dislike that they should say …). ﴿إنَّما أنْتَ نَذِيرٌ﴾, i.e. your duty is only to warn them and to bring them, of the signs, what is revealed to you; it is not your duty to bring them their desires and the signs they propose. Then He made known to them the line of argument against them, saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿أمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَراهُ﴾ [Hūd: 13], i.e. ”أيَقُولُونَ افْتَراهُ؟“ (Do they say he has fabricated it?).

zajjaj:13-13.t: ﴿قُلْ فَأْتُوا بِعَشْرِ سُوَرٍ مِثْلِهِ﴾, i.e. [each] like a sura of it, i.e. a sura of it. ﴿وادْعُوا مَنِ اسْتَطَعْتُمْ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾, i.e. seek the help in that of everyone you are able to [enlist], and whose backing and assistance you hope for.

zajjaj:14-14.t: ﴿فَإلَّمْ يَسْتَجِيبُوا لَكم فاعْلَمُوا أنَّما أُنْـزِلَ بِعِلْمِ اللَّهِ﴾ — the meaning of ”أُنْزِلَ بِعِلْمِ اللَّهِ“ is: "It was sent down while Allah knows of its being sent down", and knows that it is truth from Him. It may also be — and Allah knows best — that ”بِعِلْمِ اللَّهِ“ means: "with what Allah has announced in it of the unseen, and [with which] He has pointed to what will be and what has passed, of which the Prophet ﷺ had not read in any book"; and this is a proof that it is from Allah.

zajjaj:15-15.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿مَن كانَ يُرِيدُ الحَياةَ الدُّنْيا وزِينَتَها نُوَفِّ إلَيْهِمْ أعْمالَهم فِيها﴾, i.e. We requite them for their deeds in this world. As for ”كانَ“ in the chapter of the particles of condition (ḥurūf al-jazāʾ), there are two views on it. Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: it may, because of its strength in the sense of pastness, be an expression for every past verb; this is its strength. In the same way one interprets His saying: ﴿إنْ كُنْتُ قُلْتُهُ فَقَدْ عَلِمْتَهُ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 116].
Its true sense — and Allah knows best — is: "whoever you know this of"; so this follows the pattern of all other verbs, except that the meaning of ”كانَ“ is a report about the state in past time. When you say ”سَيَكُونُ عالِمًا“ (he will be knowledgeable), you have announced that his state will occur in the future. So the meaning of ”كانَ“ and ”يَكُونُ“ is only an expression for actions and states.

zajjaj:17-17.t:
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿أفَمَن كانَ عَلى بَيِّنَةٍ مِن رَبِّهِ ويَتْلُوهُ شاهِدٌ مِنهُ﴾ — it is said in the tafsīr that He means Muhammad ﷺ. ﴿وَيَتْلُوهُ شاهِدٌ مِنهُ﴾, i.e. a witness from his Lord, and the witness is Gabriel. It has also been said: the proof (burhān) follows it — [i.e.] that which was mentioned as the clear evidence (bayyina) — because bayyina and burhān have one meaning.
It has also been said: ”وَيَتْلُوهُ شاهِدٌ مِنهُ“ means the tongue of the Prophet ﷺ, i.e. "Is the one who is upon clear evidence from his Lord, and has with him such excellence as makes that evidence clear, equal to others?!" Mention of his opposite was left out because what comes after it points to it, as in His saying: ﴿مَثَلُ الفَرِيقَيْنِ كالأعْمى والأصَمِّ والبَصِيرِ والسَّمِيعِ﴾ [Hūd: 24].
It may also be — and Allah knows best — that by ”أفَمَن كانَ عَلى بَيِّنَةٍ مِن رَبِّهِ“ He means the Prophet ﷺ and the rest of the believers, and that the meaning of ”وَيَتْلُوهُ شاهِدٌ مِنهُ“ is: it follows it and comes after it, i.e. a witness from that clarification follows the clarification. The proof for this view would be: ﴿أُولَئِكَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ﴾,
and its proof would also be: ﴿الر كِتابٌ أُحْكِمَتْ آياتُهُ ثُمَّ فُصِّلَتْ﴾ [Hūd: 1]; the witness following after the clarification is like the detailing following after the making firm.
His saying: ﴿وَمِن قَبْلِهِ كِتابُ مُوسى إمامًا ورَحْمَةً﴾, i.e. and before this there was the Book of Moses as evidence for the matter of the Prophet ﷺ. ﴿كِتابُ مُوسى﴾ is by conjunction (ʿaṭf) with His saying: "and a witness from Him follows it, and before it the Book of Moses", i.e. and the Book of Moses was following it,
because Moses and Jesus gave glad tidings of the Prophet in the Torah and the Gospel. Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ الرَّسُولَ النَّبِيَّ الأُمِّيَّ الَّذِي يَجِدُونَهُ مَكْتُوبًا عِنْدَهم في التَّوْراةِ والإنْجِيلِ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 157]. ”إمامًا“ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because ﴿كِتابُ مُوسى﴾ is definite. ﴿فَلا تَكُ في مِرْيَةٍ مِنهُ﴾:
it is permissible to give kasra or ḍamma to the mīm in ”مِرْيَةٍ“, and both have been read in ”مِرْيَةٍ“, as with ”فِرْيَةٌ“. The accusative of ﴿كِتابُ مُوسى﴾ is also permissible, the meaning being: "and a witness from Him follows it, and he is the one who used to recite the Book of Moses". The better is the nominative, and the reading is with the nominative and nothing else.

zajjaj:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ يُعْرَضُونَ عَلى رَبِّهِمْ ويَقُولُ الأشْهادُ هَؤُلاءِ الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا عَلى رَبِّهِمْ﴾ — the ashhād (witnesses) are the prophets and the believers. He said ﴿أُولَئِكَ يُعْرَضُونَ عَلى رَبِّهِمْ﴾ although all creation will be presented to their Lord — as He said, exalted is His praise, ”إلَيْنا مَرْجِعُهم“ (to Us is their return) and ”إلَيْنا يُرْجَعُونَ“ (to Us they will be returned) — so He mentioned their being presented to their Lord as emphasis of their state with regard to the vengeance taken on them.
His saying: ﴿ألا لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ عَلى الظّالِمِينَ﴾ — ”لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ“ (Allah's curse) is His removing whomever He curses far from His pardon and His mercy.

zajjaj:19-19.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ ويَبْغُونَها عِوَجًا﴾, i.e. they turn [people] away from the path of faith in the Prophet ﷺ, wanting to turn the path — which is faith and straightness — into disbelief and deviation from the right course. ﴿وَهم بِالآخِرَةِ هم كافِرُونَ﴾ — ”هُمْ“ is mentioned a second time by way of tawkīd (emphasis) of their condition in disbelief.

zajjaj:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ لَمْ يَكُونُوا مُعْجِزِينَ في الأرْضِ﴾, i.e. taking vengeance in the abode of this world does not escape Allah's power, and there is no protector who can prevent Allah's vengeance on whomever He wills to punish. Then He began anew (istaʾnafa) and said: ﴿يُضاعَفُ لَهُمُ العَذابُ﴾, describing the doubling of the punishment in proportion to what He described of the enormity of their disbelief in His Prophet ﷺ and in the resurrection and the raising.
﴿ما كانُوا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ السَّمْعَ وما كانُوا يُبْصِرُونَ﴾, i.e. because of the intensity of their disbelief and their enmity toward the Prophet ﷺ they cannot bear to listen to what he says. Then He — Majestic and Mighty is He — made clear the harm of that to them, saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أنْفُسَهم وضَلَّ عَنْهم ما كانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ﴾ [Hūd: 21].

zajjaj:3-3.t: His saying: ﴿وَأنِ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ﴾, i.e. "and I command you to seek forgiveness", ﴿ثُمَّ تُوبُوا إلَيْهِ يُمَتِّعْكم مَتاعًا حَسَنًا﴾, i.e. He will keep you alive and not extirpate you with punishment as He extirpated the people of the towns who disbelieved. ﴿وَيُؤْتِ كُلَّ ذِي فَضْلٍ فَضْلَهُ﴾, i.e. whoever has merit in his religion, Allah will give him preference with reward, and give him preference in rank in this world through religion, as He gave preference to the Companions of His Prophet — upon him be peace.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿ألا إنَّهم يَثْنُونَ صُدُورَهم لِيَسْتَخْفُوا مِنهُ﴾ — ”ألا“ means alerting (tanbīh), and has no share in the i'rab; what comes after it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) [Translator's note: i.e. a new sentence begins after it]. The meaning of ”يَثْنُونَ صُدُورَهم لِيَسْتَخْفُوا“ is: they conceal enmity toward the Prophet ﷺ.
It has also been said that a group of the polytheists said: "When we lock our doors, let down our curtains, wrap ourselves in our garments and fold our breasts over enmity toward Muhammad ﷺ, how will he know about us?" So He — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known what they concealed, and said — exalted is His praise —: ﴿ألا حِينَ يَسْتَغْشُونَ ثِيابَهم يَعْلَمُ ما يُسِرُّونَ وما يُعْلِنُونَ﴾.
It has been read: ”ألا إنَّهم يَثْنَوْنِي صُدُورُهُمْ“ — al-Aʿmash read it so — and it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās: ”تَثْنَوْنِي صُدُورُهُمْ“, on the pattern ”تَفْعَوْعِلُ“. Its meaning is intensiveness in the thing; like it is ”قَدِ احْلَوْلى الشَّيْءُ“ (the thing has become very sweet), when it reaches the utmost in sweetness.

zajjaj:6-6.t:
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿وَيَعْلَمُ مُسْتَقَرَّها ومُسْتَوْدَعَها﴾ — it has been said: ”مُسْتَقَرُّها“ is its abode on the face of the earth, and ”مُسْتَوْدَعُها“ is what it ends up in. It has also been said: ”مُسْتَقَرُّها“ is in the loins, and ”مُسْتَوْدَعُها“ is in the wombs.
His saying: ﴿كُلٌّ في كِتابٍ مُبِينٍ﴾, i.e. that is established in Allah's knowledge, and it may be that it is in a book; likewise His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿إلا في كِتابٍ مِن قَبْلِ أنْ نَبْرَأها﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 22].

zajjaj:7-7.t:
His saying: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ والأرْضَ في سِتَّةِ أيّامٍ﴾ — Allah is able to create them in an instant, because He has power over all things.
And when He created them and measured them to this great extent — and the sky has no visible pillar between it and the earth — in six days, it became known that one whose power is this power is not incapacitated by anything. Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿أوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أنَّ اللَّهَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ والأرْضَ ولَمْ يَعْيَ بِخَلْقِهِنَّ بِقادِرٍ عَلى أنْ يُحْيِيَ المَوْتى﴾ [al-Aḥqāf: 33]. The polytheists used to deny that He would raise the dead, while acknowledging that He is the Creator of the heavens and the earth.
His saying: ﴿وَكانَ عَرْشُهُ عَلى الماءِ﴾ — this indicates that the Throne and the water existed before the heavens and the earth.
His saying: ﴿لِيَبْلُوَكم أيُّكم أحْسَنُ عَمَلا﴾ — its meaning is: "to test you with the test for which He will requite you, while He knew before that which of them is best in deeds", except that He requites them according to their deeds, not according to His knowledge about them.
﴿وَلَئِنْ قُلْتَ إنَّكم مَبْعُوثُونَ مِن بَعْدِ المَوْتِ لَيَقُولَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إنْ هَذا إلا سِحْرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾
It is also read: ”إلّا ساحِرٌ مُبِينٌ“ (nothing but a manifest sorcerer). Sorcery is falsehood in their view, so it is as though they said: "This is nothing but manifest falsehood." And Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known to them that the power to create the heavens and the earth points to the raising of the dead.
The people of disbelief differ about the resurrection: the polytheists say that they will not be raised at all and will not be returned after their death; the Jews and the Christians claim that there is no eating, no drinking and no intercourse with women in Paradise. Each one disbelieves in the resurrection in his own way.

zajjaj:8-8.t:
﴿وَلَئِنْ أخَّرْنا عَنْهُمُ العَذابَ إلى أُمَّةٍ مَعْدُودَةٍ﴾ — its meaning is: to a term and a known period, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وادَّكَرَ بَعْدَ أُمَّةٍ﴾ [Yūsuf: 45], i.e. after a period.
His saying: ﴿ألا يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمْ لَيْسَ مَصْرُوفًا﴾ — ”يَوْمَ يَأْتِيهِمْ“ is accusative (manṣūb) by ”مَصْرُوفًا“. The meaning: the punishment will not be turned away from them on the day it comes to them.
﴿وَحاقَ بِهِمْ ما كانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ﴾ — as you say: ”أحاطَ بِفُلانٍ عَمَلُهُ“ (his deeds encompassed so-and-so) and ”أهْلَكَهُ كَسْبُهُ“ (his earnings destroyed him), i.e. "the recompense of his earnings and its consequence destroyed him".

zajjaj:9-9.t: His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿وَلَئِنْ أذَقْنا الإنْسانَ مِنّا رَحْمَةً ثُمَّ نَـزَعْناها مِنهُ إنَّهُ لَيَئُوسٌ كَفُورٌ﴾ — He means the disbeliever. ”اَلرَّحْمَةُ“ here is provision, and ”اَلْإنْسانُ“ is a generic noun (ism li-l-jins), in the sense of ”اَلنّاسُ“ (people).

zajjaj:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿لا جَرَمَ أنَّهم في الآخِرَةِ هُمُ الأخْسَرُونَ﴾ — the exegetes said: the meaning is "[as] a true recompense, that in the Hereafter they are the greatest losers". Sībawayh held that ”جَرَمَ“ means ”حَقٌّ“ (it is true / it is due). The poet said:
؎وَلَقَدْ طَعَنْتُ أبا عُيَيْنَةَ طَعْنَةً جَرَمَتْ فَزارَةَ بَعْدَها أنْ يَغْضَبُوا
(I struck Abū ʿUyayna such a thrust that after it Fazāra were bound to be angry.)
Its meaning is: "The thrust made Fazāra deserving of anger." The meaning of ”لا“ is negation of what they thought would benefit them, as though the meaning were: "That will not benefit them; it is due (jarama) that in the Hereafter they are the greatest losers", i.e. "that deed has earned them loss".

zajjaj:24-24.t: Then Allah struck a parable for the believers and the disbelievers, saying: ﴿مَثَلُ الفَرِيقَيْنِ كالأعْمى والأصَمِّ والبَصِيرِ والسَّمِيعِ﴾. The likeness of the party of the disbelievers is as the blind and the deaf, because in their enmity and their abandoning of understanding they are like one who neither hears nor sees.

zajjaj:25-25.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أرْسَلْنا نُوحًا إلى قَوْمِهِ إنِّي لَكم نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ — ”إنَّ“ is with kasra in the reading, in the sense of: "He said to them: I am to you a clear warner." ”أنِّي لَكم نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ“ (with fatḥa) is also permissible, in the sense of: "We sent Noah to his people with warning, that you worship none but Allah — I warn you so that you will affirm the Oneness of Allah and abandon the worship of others." ﴿إنِّي أخافُ عَلَيْكم عَذابَ يَوْمٍ ألِيمٍ﴾ [Hūd: 26]:
outside the [established] reading, ”إنِّي أخافُ عَلَيْكم عَذابَ يَوْمٍ ألِيمًا“ is permissible, because al-alīm (painful) is a ṣifa (adjective) of the punishment. He described the day with pain only because pain occurs in it. The meaning is: "the punishment of a muʾlim (pain-giving) day", i.e. a hurtful one.

zajjaj:27-27.t:
﴿فَقالَ المَلأُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِن قَوْمِهِ﴾ — ”اَلْمَلَأُ“ are the chiefs of the people and their great ones, who are full (mulāʾ) of counsel and of what is needed from them; i.e. they answered him with this answer and saying: ﴿ما نَراكَ إلا بَشَرًا مِثْلَنا﴾, i.e. "We see you as nothing but a human being like us", ﴿وَما نَراكَ اتَّبَعَكَ إلا الَّذِينَ هم أراذِلُنا﴾, i.e. the notables among us have not followed you; only the basest of us have followed you.
His saying: ﴿بادِيَ الرَّأْيِ﴾ — without hamza in ”بادِي“; Abū ʿAmr pronounces it with hamza: ”بادِئَ الرَّأْيِ“. [Without hamza] it means: "they followed [you] a following in what is outwardly seen" — this is for whoever does not pronounce the hamza. The interpretation in this is of two kinds: one of them is "they followed you outwardly, while inwardly they are otherwise".
It may also be: "they followed you on the surface of opinion, without reflecting on what you said or thinking about it". The reading of Abū ʿAmr is on this second interpretation, i.e. "they followed you at the outset of opinion", i.e. when they first began to look; and when they reflected they did not follow you. As for the accusative of ”بادِيَ الرَّأْيِ“, it is on [the sense of] "they followed you in the outward [appearance] of opinion" and "upon the outward [appearance] of opinion", as though he said: "the following which they did not think about". Whoever says ”بادِيَ الرَّأْيِ“ makes it accusative on that basis.

zajjaj:28-28.t:
﴿قالَ يا قَوْمِ أرَأيْتُمْ إنْ كُنْتُ عَلى بَيِّنَةٍ مِن رَبِّي وآتانِي رَحْمَةً مِن عِنْدِهِ فَعُمِّيَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ — so is most of the reading, with fatḥa on the ʿayn and without doubling [Translator's note: i.e. فَعَمِيَتْ; the verse as printed in the source shows the other reading]; and it has also been read ”فَعُمِّيَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ“, with ḍamma on the ʿayn and doubling of the mīm. This is what he answered them with when they said: "Those who followed you followed you without verifying." So with this saying he made known to them that they were verifying, because if he is upon clear evidence, then whoever believed in him is knowing, perceptive and favoured [with that], and whoever did not grasp the clear evidence — the right course has been made blind to him.
His saying: ﴿فَعُمِّيَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾, i.e. the clear evidence has been obscured to you. ﴿أنُلْزِمُكُمُوها﴾: the reading is with ḍamma on the mīm; making it quiescent (iskān) is permissible though far-fetched, because of the many vowels and the heaviness of ḍamma after kasra. Sībawayh and al-Khalīl do not permit making the inflectional letter (ḥarf al-iʿrāb) quiescent except under [poetic] necessity. As for the quiescence related from Abū ʿAmr, that was not accurately recorded from him; Sībawayh related from him that he used to lighten the vowels and slur them (ikhtilās), and this is the correct view.

zajjaj:29-29.t: His saying: ﴿وَما أنا بِطارِدِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إنَّهم مُلاقُو رَبِّهِمْ﴾ — when they meet their Lord, He will requite whoever wronged them and drove them away with His requital of punishment.

zajjaj:31-31.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلا أقُولُ لِلَّذِينَ تَزْدَرِي أعْيُنُكم لَنْ يُؤْتِيَهُمُ اللَّهُ خَيْرًا﴾ — ”تَزْدَرِي“ means: [your eyes] look down upon and deem base. One says ”زَرَيْتُ عَلى الرَّجُلِ“ when you find fault with him and deem his deed base, and ”أزْرَيْتُ“ when you belittle him. The origin of ”تَزْدَرِي“ is ”تَزْتَرِي“, with tāʾ, except that this tāʾ is changed into dāl after zāy, because tāʾ is one of the whispered (mahmūs, voiceless) letters, and the whispered letters are faint, so the tāʾ after zāy becomes obscured; hence dāl was substituted for it because of its voicedness (jahr). Likewise ”يَفْتَعِلُ“ from ”اَلزِّينَةُ“ (adornment) is ”يَزْدانُ“; you say: ”أنْتَ تَزْدانُ يا هَذا“ (You adorn yourself, you there).
His saying: ﴿وَلا أقُولُ لِلَّذِينَ تَزْدَرِي أعْيُنُكم لَنْ يُؤْتِيَهُمُ اللَّهُ خَيْرًا﴾ [was said] because they had said: "The basest of us have followed you."
His saying: ﴿اللَّهُ أعْلَمُ بِما في أنْفُسِهِمْ﴾, i.e. if you claim that they followed me only on the surface of opinion — what I call to is the Oneness of Allah; so when I see someone who affirms the Oneness of Allah — exalted is His praise — I act on his outward state, and Allah knows best what is in his soul; none knows the unseen except Allah.

zajjaj:32-32.t: His saying: ﴿فَأكْثَرْتَ جِدالَنا﴾ — and it is read: ”فَأكْثَرْتَ جَدَلَنا“. ”اَلْجَدَلُ“ and ”اَلْجِدالُ“ mean going to extremes in disputing and contending. It is taken from ”اَلْجَدْلُ“, which is tight twisting [of a rope]; and the falcon is called ”أجْدَلُ“ because it is among the strongest of birds.

zajjaj:34-34.t: His saying: ﴿إنْ كانَ اللَّهُ يُرِيدُ أنْ يُغْوِيَكُمْ﴾ — ”يُغْوِيَكُمْ“ means: to lead you astray and destroy you.

zajjaj:35-35.t: His saying: ﴿أمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَراهُ﴾ — its meaning is: ”بَلْ أيَقُولُونَ افْتَراهُ؟!“ (Rather, do they say he fabricated it?!). ﴿قُلْ إنِ افْتَرَيْتُهُ فَعَلَيَّ إجْرامِي﴾ is from your saying ”أجْرَمَ الرَّجُلُ إجْرامًا“ (the man committed a crime). One also says ”جَرَمَ“ in the sense of ”أجْرَمَ“, and ”أجْرَمَ“ is mostly used specifically for earning sin. One says: ”رَجُلٌ مُجْرِمٌ، وجارِمٌ“ (a criminal man). ”فَعَلَيَّ أجْرامِي“ is also permissible, as the plural of ”جُرْمٌ“; it is like His saying ﴿واللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ إسْرارَهُمْ﴾ [Muḥammad: 26] and ”أسْرارَهُمْ“, except that the reading is with kasra on the alif, ”إجْرامِي“, as a maṣdar (verbal noun).

zajjaj:36-36.t:
﴿وَأُوحِيَ إلى نُوحٍ أنَّهُ لَنْ يُؤْمِنَ مِن قَوْمِكَ إلا مَن قَدْ آمَنَ﴾ — for that reason — and Allah knows best — Noah sought refuge [in Allah] with his saying: ﴿لا تَذَرْ عَلى الأرْضِ مِنَ الكافِرِينَ دَيّارًا﴾ [Nūḥ: 26] ﴿إنَّكَ إنْ تَذَرْهم يُضِلُّوا عِبادَكَ ولا يَلِدُوا إلا فاجِرًا كَفّارًا﴾ [Nūḥ: 27].
He was made to know that they would beget none but disbelievers by His saying, the Exalted: ﴿أنَّهُ لَنْ يُؤْمِنَ مِن قَوْمِكَ إلا مَن قَدْ آمَنَ فَلا تَبْتَئِسْ بِما كانُوا يَفْعَلُونَ﴾ — its meaning is: "Do not grieve and do not be abased."

zajjaj:37-37.t: His saying: ﴿واصْنَعِ الفُلْكَ بِأعْيُنِنا﴾ — ”اَلْفُلْكُ“ is the ship. ”اَلْفَلَكُ“ [Translator's note: so vowelled in the source; the discussion concerns al-fulk] can be singular and can be plural, just as they said ”أسَدٌ“ and ”أُسْدٌ“ (lion, lions); they said in the singular ”فَلَكٌ“ and in the plural ”فُلْكٌ“, because fuʿl and faʿal have one plural, and they often come with one meaning. One says ”اَلْعُجْمُ“ and ”اَلْعَجَمُ“ (non-Arabs), ”اَلْعُرْبُ“ and ”اَلْعَرَبُ“ (Arabs), and ”اَلْفُلْكُ“ and ”اَلْفَلَكُ“; and ”اَلْفَلْكَةُ“ is said of anything round or with roundness in it. The meaning of ﴿بِأعْيُنِنا ووَحْيِنا﴾ is: with Our watching over you and Our guarding of you, and with what We revealed to you. ﴿وَلا تُخاطِبْنِي في الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا إنَّهم مُغْرَقُونَ﴾ — the meaning: "Do not address Me concerning respite for those who disbelieved; they will be drowned."

zajjaj:38-38.t: Then Allah — exalted is His praise — told of his making the ship, saying: ﴿وَيَصْنَعُ الفُلْكَ وكُلَّما مَرَّ عَلَيْهِ مَلأٌ مِن قَوْمِهِ سَخِرُوا مِنهُ﴾. It is said in the tafsīr that they used to say: "This one who claims that he is a prophet sent [by Allah] has become a carpenter." So he said: ﴿إنْ تَسْخَرُوا مِنّا فَإنّا نَسْخَرُ مِنكم كَما تَسْخَرُونَ﴾, i.e. we deem you ignorant as you deem us ignorant.

zajjaj:39-39.t: Then he made known to them what the outcome of their affair would be, saying: ﴿فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ مَن يَأْتِيهِ عَذابٌ يُخْزِيهِ ويَحِلُّ عَلَيْهِ عَذابٌ مُقِيمٌ﴾, i.e. you will come to know who is more deserving of disgrace, and who has the more praiseworthy outcome.

zajjaj:40-40.t:
﴿حَتّى إذا جاءَ أمْرُنا وفارَ التَّنُّورُ﴾ — Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — made known to Noah that the time of their destruction would be the boiling up of the tannūr. Several views have been given about the tannūr. It has been said that the tannūr is the face of the earth; it is said that the water boiled up from the direction of the mosque of Kufa; it is said that the water boiled up from the oven (tannūr) of the woman baking bread; and it has been said: ”اَلتَّنُّورُ“ is the shining (tanwīr) of dawn.
In sum, the water boiled up from the earth and came from the sky. Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿فَفَتَحْنا أبْوابَ السَّماءِ بِماءٍ مُنْهَمِرٍ﴾ [al-Qamar: 11] ﴿وَفَجَّرْنا الأرْضَ عُيُونًا فالتَقى الماءُ عَلى أمْرٍ قَدْ قُدِرَ﴾ [al-Qamar: 12]. So the water's boiling up — whether from an oven, from the direction of the mosque, from the face of the earth, or at the time of dawn — does not preclude that being the sign for the destruction of the people. ﴿قُلْنا احْمِلْ فِيها مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ﴾, i.e. of every thing.
”اَلزَّوْجُ“ in the speech of the Arabs is one [individual], which may have another one with it; and the two together are called ”زَوْجانِ“. A man says: ”عَلَيَّ زَوْجانِ مِنَ الخِفافِ“ (I am wearing a pair of khuffs), and you say: ”عِنْدِي زَوْجانِ مِنَ الطَّيْرِ“ (I have a pair of birds), whereas you mean [by zawj] only a male or a female. It is also read: ”مِن كُلِّ زَوْجَيْنِ“, as a genitive construct (iḍāfa).
The meaning is the same for ”the two zawj“, whether you make it a construct or not. ﴿وَأهْلَكَ إلا مَن سَبَقَ عَلَيْهِ القَوْلُ ومَن آمَنَ﴾, i.e. "and carry whoever has believed". It is said: "Those who believed with him were eighty souls"; so He, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَما آمَنَ مَعَهُ إلا قَلِيلٌ﴾, because eighty is few within the whole nation of Noah's people.

zajjaj:41-41.t:
﴿وَقالَ ارْكَبُوا فِيها بِسْمِ اللَّهِ مَجْراها ومُرْساها﴾, i.e. by Allah it sails and by Him it comes to rest. The meaning of ”قُلْنا بِاسْمِ اللَّهِ“ [Translator's note: so in the source] is: "by Allah". It has been read in several ways: it has been read ”مَجْراها“ with fatḥa on the mīm and ”مُرْساها“ with ḍamma on the mīm.
It has also been read ”مُجْراها ومُرْساها“, with ḍamma on both mīms; and ”مَجْراها ومَرْساها“ is permissible. All are correct and good. As for whoever read ”مَجْراها“ with fatḥa on the mīm, the meaning is "its sailing", and ”مُرْساها“ means: "and by Allah its anchoring takes place", i.e. its being brought to rest.
Whoever read ”مُجْراها ومُرْساها“, the meaning of that is: "by Allah is its being made to sail, and by Allah is its being anchored"; one says ”أجْرَيْتُهُ مُجْرًى، وإجْراءً“ (I made it run), with one meaning. Whoever said ”مَجْراها ومَرْساها“, it is on [the pattern] ”جَرَتْ جَرْيًا، ومَجْرًى“ (it ran) and ”رَسَتْ رُسُوًّا ومَرْسًى“ (it came to rest).
”اَلْمَرْسى“ is its resting place. The meaning is that Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — commanded them to say the name [of Allah] at the time of its sailing and the time of its coming to rest. ”مُرْساها“ is in the position of the genitive as a ṣifa (adjective) of Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — [Translator's note: so in the source; the forms that would be adjectives of Allah are the participles ”مُجْرِيها ومُرْسِيها“ discussed next]. There is something permissible in it that has not been read — and it should not be read, because the reading is a followed sunna (practice): ”بِاسْمِ اللَّهِ مُجْرِيَها“, in two ways. One of them is the ḥāl (circumstantial), the meaning being "making it sail and making it rest", as you say ”مَرَرْتُ بِزَيْدٍ ضارِبَها“ (I passed by Zayd, striking her), as a ḥāl. It may also be accusative by way of praise (al-madḥ): "I mean: the One who makes it sail and makes it rest". It may also be that ”مُجْرِيها ومُرْسِيها“ is in the position of the nominative, with ”هُوَ مُجْرِيها ومُرْسِيها“ (He is the One who makes it sail and makes it rest) implied.

zajjaj:42-42.t:
His saying: ﴿وَهِيَ تَجْرِي بِهِمْ في مَوْجٍ كالجِبالِ﴾ — it has been said that the waters of the sky and the earth met and closed over the space between them, and the ship sailed in that water.
His saying: ﴿وَهِيَ تَجْرِي بِهِمْ في مَوْجٍ كالجِبالِ﴾ — waves occur only on top of the water; and it has come in the tafsīr that the water exceeded everything by fifteen cubits.
Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿فالتَقى الماءُ عَلى أمْرٍ قَدْ قُدِرَ﴾ [al-Qamar: 12]. So it is possible that the water of the sky and the water of the earth met without what is between them being filled up, and it is possible that what is between them was filled up. ”اَلْمَوْجُ“ is the surging of the water, and its formation is mostly known to be in the upper part of the water,
but it is possible for it to surge inside the water. As for the reports about the ship, the most that has been said about its length is that it was one thousand two hundred cubits; it has also been said: "six hundred cubits". It has been said that Noah was sent when he was forty years old, and remained among his people, as Allah — exalted is His praise — said, ﴿ألْفَ سَنَةٍ إلا خَمْسِينَ عامًا﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 14]; he built the ship in fifty years, and lived after the Flood sixty years.
﴿وَنادى نُوحٌ ابْنَهُ وكانَ في مَعْزِلٍ﴾ — it may be that he was apart from his religion, i.e. his father's religion; and it may be — and this is more likely — that he was apart from the ship. ﴿يا بُنَيَّ ارْكَبْ مَعَنا﴾: the kasra is the best reading, I mean kasra on the yāʾ. Both kasra and fatḥa are permissible, [each] from two directions. [For the kasra:] one of them is that the origin is ”يا بُنَيِّي“, and the yāʾ is dropped in the vocative — I mean the yāʾ of the possessive (yāʾ al-iḍāfa) — while the kasra remains to indicate it.
[The other is that] the yāʾ may be dropped because of the quiescence of the rāʾ in ”اِرْكَبْ“, and it is left in writing as it is in pronunciation. The fatḥa is from two directions: [one,] the origin is ”يا بُنَيّا“, the alif being substituted for the possessive yāʾ — the Arabs say ”يا غُلامًا أقْبِلْ“ (O my boy, come forward) — then the alif is dropped because of its quiescence and the quiescence of the rāʾ, and it is left in writing according to its being dropped in pronunciation.
[The other:] the vocative alif may be dropped just as the possessive yāʾ is dropped. The possessive yāʾ and the possessive alif are dropped in the vocative only as tanwīn (nunation) is dropped, because the possessive yāʾ is an addition to the noun, just as tanwīn is an addition to it. Another aspect is permissible which has not been read, namely retaining the yāʾ: ”يا بُنَيِّي“; this is heavy because of the coming together of the yāʾs.

zajjaj:43-43.t:
﴿قالَ سَآوِي إلى جَبَلٍ يَعْصِمُنِي مِنَ الماءِ﴾, i.e. it will protect me from the water, meaning: from the water's drowning [me]. ﴿قالَ لا عاصِمَ اليَوْمَ مِن أمْرِ اللَّهِ إلا مَن رَحِمَ﴾ — this is an exception not from the first [category] (disjunctive exception), and the position of ”مَن“ is accusative. The meaning: "but whomever Allah has mercy on, he is protected". ”لا عاصِمَ“ may mean ”لا ذا عِصْمَةٍ“ (no one possessed of protection), as they said ”عِيشَةٌ راضِيَةٌ“, whose meaning is murḍiya (a pleasing life); ”راضِيَةٌ“ is allowed by way of relation (nasab), i.e. in a life possessing contentment.
On this interpretation ”مَن“ is in the position of the nominative, and the meaning is: "No one is protected except the one shown mercy."
His saying: ﴿وَغِيضَ الماءُ﴾ [Hūd: 44] — one says ”غاضَ الماءُ، يَغِيضُ“ when water sinks into the earth; giving the ghayn a trace of ḍamma (ishmām) is permissible. ﴿وَقُضِيَ الأمْرُ﴾ [Hūd: 44], i.e. the destruction of Noah's people. ﴿واسْتَوَتْ عَلى الجُودِيِّ﴾ [Hūd: 44]: ”اَلْجُودِيُّ“ is a mountain in the region of Āmid.

zajjaj:45-45.t:
His saying: ﴿فَقالَ رَبِّ إنَّ ابْنِي مِن أهْلِي وإنَّ وعْدَكَ الحَقُّ وأنْتَ أحْكَمُ الحاكِمِينَ﴾ ﴿قالَ يا نُوحُ إنَّهُ لَيْسَ مِن أهْلِكَ إنَّهُ عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صالِحٍ﴾ [Hūd: 46] — al-Ḥasan and Ibn Sīrīn read: ”عَمَلٌ غَيْرَ صالِحٍ“ [Translator's note: so in the source; the reading usually attributed is ”عَمِلَ غَيْرَ صالِحٍ“, "he did what was not righteous"]. Their position was that he was not his son, not having been born of his loins. Al-Ḥasan said: "By Allah, he was not his son." Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd said: "He was his son, and Allah never tried a prophet in his family with a trial like this." As for whoever read ”إنَّهُ عَمَلٌ غَيْرُ صالِحٍ“, it may be that he means by it that he is "one possessed of unrighteous deeds", as al-Khansāʾ said:
؎تَرْتَعُ ما رَتَعَتْ حَتّى إذا ادَّكَرَتْ فَإنَّما هي إقْبالٌ وإدْبارُ
(She grazes as long as she grazes, until when she remembers [her lost calf], she is nothing but coming and going.)
i.e. "possessed of coming". Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿وَنادى نُوحٌ ابْنَهُ﴾ [Hūd: 42], attributing him to him. But someone may say: He attributed him to him according to usage, as Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿أيْنَ شُرَكائِيَ الَّذِينَ كُنْتُمْ تُشاقُّونَ فِيهِمْ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 27], attributing them to Himself according to their saying, while Allah has no partner. However, the better interpretation is: "He is not of your family whom I promised you I would save". And ”إنَّهُ لَيْسَ مِن أهْلِكَ“ may mean: "He is not of the people of your religion."
﴿فَلا تَسْألْنِي ما لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ﴾ [Hūd: 46] — and it is read: ”فَلا تَسْألَنْ ما لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ“.

zajjaj:50-50.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإلى عادٍ أخاهم هُودًا﴾ — the meaning: "And We sent to ʿĀd their brother Hūd." ”أخاهُمْ“ (their brother) is said from two directions: one of them is that he was from among them and spoke clearly in their language; the other is that he was their brother among the children of Adam, a human being like them.
﴿قالَ يا قَوْمِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ ما لَكم مِن إلَهٍ غَيْرُهُ﴾ — and if you wish, ”غَيْرِهِ“: ”غَيْرِهِ“ (genitive) is a naʿt (adjective) of ilāh (god), and ”غَيْرُهُ“ (nominative) is on the sense of ”ما لَكم إلَهٌ غَيْرُهُ“ (you have no god other than Him).

zajjaj:52-52.t:
﴿يُرْسِلِ السَّماءَ عَلَيْكم مِدْرارًا﴾ — drought had struck them, so he made known to them that if they sought their Lord's forgiveness and repented, He would send the sky upon them in abundant rain (midrār).
”اَلتَّوْبَةُ“ (repentance) is remorse for what has passed, resolve to abandon returning to sins, and persistence in performing the obligations. ”مِدْرارًا“ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), as though He said: "He will send the sky upon you pouring (dārra)"; and the meaning of ”مِدْرارٌ“ is intensiveness.
The people of Hūd — I mean ʿĀd — were people of orchards, crops and building, and their dwellings were the sands that lie between Syria and Yemen. Hūd called them to the Oneness of Allah, to seeking His forgiveness and to abandoning the worship of idols, but they did not obey him. He threatened them with punishment, and they persisted in their disbelief; so Allah sent the wind upon them, and it would enter their noses and come out of their backsides, and cut them to pieces limb by limb.
﴿وَيَزِدْكم قُوَّةً إلى قُوَّتِكم ولا تَتَوَلَّوْا﴾, i.e. He will increase you in strength in the blessing you have; it may also be: "and He will increase you in strength in your bodies".

zajjaj:54-54.t: ﴿إنْ نَقُولُ إلا اعْتَراكَ بَعْضُ آلِهَتِنا بِسُوءٍ﴾, i.e. we say nothing but that one of our idols has touched you with madness because of your reviling them. So he said to them: ﴿إنِّي أُشْهِدُ اللَّهَ واشْهَدُوا أنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِمّا تُشْرِكُونَ﴾ ﴿مِن دُونِهِ فَكِيدُونِي جَمِيعًا ثُمَّ لا تُنْظِرُونِ﴾ [Hūd: 55]. This is among the greatest signs of the messengers: that the messenger is alone, and his nation is united against him, and he says to it: "Plot against me, then give me no respite", and not one of them is able to harm him. Likewise Noah said to his people: ﴿فَأجْمِعُوا أمْرَكم وشُرَكاءَكم ثُمَّ لا يَكُنْ أمْرُكم عَلَيْكم غُمَّةً ثُمَّ اقْضُوا إلَيَّ ولا تُنْظِرُونِ﴾ [Yūnus: 71]; and Muhammad ﷺ said: ﴿فَإنْ كانَ لَكم كَيْدٌ فَكِيدُونِ﴾ [al-Mursalāt: 39]. So this is among the greatest signs of the messengers, and the strongest proof of their messages.

zajjaj:56-56.t: ﴿ما مِن دابَّةٍ إلا هو آخِذٌ بِناصِيَتِها﴾, i.e. it is in His grasp, and His power reaches it with whatever He wills. Then he said: ﴿إنَّ رَبِّي عَلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾, i.e. He, glorified is He — even though His power reaches it with whatever He wills — wills nothing but justice.

zajjaj:57-57.t: ﴿فَإنْ تَوَلَّوْا﴾ — the meaning is ”فَإنْ تَتَوَلَّوْا“ (if you turn away). ﴿فَقَدْ أبْلَغْتُكم ما أُرْسِلْتُ بِهِ إلَيْكُمْ﴾ — he put ”فَقَدْ أبْلَغْتُكُمْ“ (I have conveyed to you) in the place of "the proof has been established against you". ﴿وَيَسْتَخْلِفُ رَبِّي قَوْمًا غَيْرَكُمْ﴾

zajjaj:58-58.t: His saying: ﴿نَجَّيْنا هُودًا والَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مَعَهُ بِرَحْمَةٍ مِنّا﴾ — it may mean: by what We showed them of guidance and clarification, which is a mercy; and it may be that ”بِرَحْمَةٍ مِّنّا“ means: no one is saved, however hard he strives, except by a mercy from Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He. ﴿وَنَجَّيْناهم مِن عَذابٍ غَلِيظٍ﴾, i.e. from that with which the disbelieving people of ʿĀd were punished in this world, and from that with which they will be punished in the Hereafter.

zajjaj:60-60.t: ﴿ألا بُعْدًا لِعادٍ قَوْمِ هُودٍ﴾ — ”ألا“ is [a particle of] opening and alerting (tanbīh). ”بُعْدًا“ is accusative on [the implied] ”أبْعَدَهُمُ اللَّهُ بُعْدًا“ (may Allah remove them far away) [i.e. as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object)] [Translator's note: the bracketed term is added for clarity]. The meaning of ”بُعْدًا“ is: far from the mercy of Allah.

zajjaj:61-61.t:
﴿وَإلى ثَمُودَ أخاهم صالِحًا﴾ — the meaning: "And We sent to Thamūd their brother Ṣāliḥ." ”ثَمُودَ“ is a diptote (does not take tanwīn) because it is the name of a tribe; whoever makes it the name of the clan (ḥayy) gives it full declension. It has come in the Quran fully declined: ”ألا إنَّ ثَمُودًا كَفَرُوا رَبَّهُمْ“.
﴿قَدْ جاءَتْكم بَيِّنَةٌ مِن رَبِّكُمْ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 73]

zajjaj:64-64.t:
Then he made clear what it [the clear sign] is, saying: ﴿هَذِهِ ناقَةُ اللَّهِ لَكم آيَةً﴾. It is said that she came out of a rock, and in this is the greatest of signs. It is also said that she used to come to the water, and no beast would come to the water with her; then on the day she did not come, all the [other] animals came to drink. In this is the greatest sign. ”آيَةً“ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). The meaning: if he said "This is the she-camel of Allah, as a sign" [or] "a sign for you" [Translator's note: so in the source], it is as though he said: "Pay attention to her in this state." ”اَلْآيَةُ“ is the sign (ʿalāma). ﴿فَذَرُوها تَأْكُلْ في أرْضِ اللَّهِ﴾,
and ”تَأْكُلُ في أرْضِ اللَّهِ“: whoever read ”تَأْكُلْ“ in the jussive (jazm), it is the answer to the command; we have explained its like in Sūrat al-Baqara. Whoever read ”تَأْكُلُ“, its meaning is: "leave her in the state of her eating". There is another aspect for the nominative, as a new sentence (istiʾnāf), the meaning being: "for she eats in Allah's earth". ﴿وَلا تَمَسُّوها بِسُوءٍ فَيَأْخُذَكم عَذابٌ قَرِيبٌ﴾ — ”فَيَأْخُذَكُمْ“ is the answer to the prohibition. The meaning is: "a punishment that comes near to whoever touches her with harm", i.e. if you hamstring her you will not be given respite.

zajjaj:65-65.t: ﴿فَعَقَرُوها فَقالَ تَمَتَّعُوا في دارِكم ثَلاثَةَ أيّامٍ ذَلِكَ وعْدٌ غَيْرُ مَكْذُوبٍ﴾ — so they were destroyed after the three [days]. We have explained in [Sūrat] al-Aʿrāf how they were destroyed.

zajjaj:68-68.t: His saying: ﴿كَأنْ لَمْ يَغْنَوْا فِيها﴾ — its meaning is: as though they had never dwelt in it. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: ”اَلْمَغانِي“ are the dwellings in which they lived. One says: ”غَنِينا بِمَكانِ كَذا وكَذا“ (we dwelt in such-and-such a place), when they stayed there.

zajjaj:69-69.t:
His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿وَلَقَدْ جاءَتْ رُسُلُنا إبْراهِيمَ بِالبُشْرى﴾ — ”بِالبُشْرى“ means: with [the glad tidings of] the child. ﴿قالُوا سَلامًا قالَ سَلامٌ﴾ — and ”قالُوا سَلامٌ“: both are read. As for His saying ”سَلامًا“, it is accusative on [the implied] ”سَلَّمْنا سَلامًا“ (we greet with a greeting of peace); as for ”سَلامٌ“, it is nominative in the sense of ”أمْرِي سَلامٌ“ (my affair is peace),
i.e. I want nothing but peace and forbearance. ﴿فَما لَبِثَ أنْ جاءَ بِعِجْلٍ حَنِيذٍ﴾, i.e. "he did not stay [long] until he brought a roasted calf". ”اَلْحَنِيذُ“ is that which is roasted on [heated] stones. It has also been said: ”اَلْحَنِيذُ“ is that which is roasted until it drips; the Arabs say ”اِحْنِذِ الفَرَسَ“, i.e. put the blanket on it until it drips with sweat. It has been said: ”اَلْحَنِيذُ“ is simply what is roasted; and it has been said: ”اَلْحَنِيذُ“ is al-samīṭ (scalded and roasted with the skin on). One says: ”حَنَذَتْهُ الشَّمْسُ، والنّارُ“ (the sun / the fire roasted it), when it roasts it.

zajjaj:70-70.t: ﴿فَلَمّا رَأى أيْدِيَهم لا تَصِلُ إلَيْهِ نَكِرَهُمْ﴾ — they did not eat because they were angels. It is said that among them the sign concerning guests, when they came intending good, was eating. One says: ”نَكِرْتُ الشَّيْءَ، وأنْكَرْتُ“ (I found the thing strange); ”نَكِرَ“ is rare in the language, and ”مَنكُورٌ“ is rare; the [usual] speech is ”أنْكَرَ“ and ”مُنْكَرٌ“. ﴿وَأوْجَسَ مِنهم خِيفَةً﴾ — its meaning is: he concealed fear of them. ﴿قالُوا لا تَخَفْ إنّا أُرْسِلْنا إلى قَوْمِ لُوطٍ﴾ — do you not see that He said in another place: ﴿إنّا أُرْسِلْنا إلى قَوْمٍ مُجْرِمِينَ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 32] ﴿لِنُرْسِلَ عَلَيْهِمْ حِجارَةً مِن طِينٍ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 33].

zajjaj:71-71.t:
﴿وامْرَأتُهُ قائِمَةٌ فَضَحِكَتْ فَبَشَّرْناها﴾ — it is related that she laughed because she had said to Abraham: "Take Lot, your brother's son, to yourself, for I know that punishment will descend upon these people." So she laughed with joy when the matter turned out as she had supposed.
As for whoever said ”ضَحِكَتْ“ means "she menstruated", that is nothing. ﴿فَبَشَّرْناها بِإسْحاقَ ومِن وراءِ إسْحاقَ يَعْقُوبَ﴾ — it is read ”يَعْقُوبُ“ and ”يَعْقُوبَ“, with the nominative and the accusative.
In this glad tiding there is glad tiding of a child and of a grandchild. One says: ”هَذا ابْنِي مِنَ الوَراءِ“, i.e. "this is my son's son". So We gave her the glad tidings that she would bear Isaac and that she would live until she saw his child. We have related in the tafsīr that her age was eighty-nine, and Abraham's age was ninety-nine, at the time of the glad tidings.
As for whoever read ”وَمِن وراءِ إسْحاقَ يَعْقُوبَ“, ”يَعْقُوبَ“ is in the position of the accusative, construed on the position of ﴿فَبَشَّرْناها بِإسْحاقَ﴾, construed on the sense; the meaning is: "We granted her Isaac, and We granted her Jacob". Whoever read ”يَعْقُوبُ“, its nominative is of two kinds. One of them is as a mubtadaʾ (subject) placed later, whose sense is that it is placed first,
the meaning being: "and Jacob is brought into being for her after Isaac". It may also be nominative by the verb that governs ”مِن وراءِ“, as though He said: "and there is established for her, after Isaac, Jacob". Whoever claims that Jacob is in the position of the genitive, his claim is wrong; that is because the preposition may not be separated from its genitive noun, nor [may the genitive be separated] from the conjoining wāw. It is not permissible [to say] ”مَرَرْتُ بِزَيْدٍ فِي الدّارِ، والبَيْتِ عَمْرٍو“, nor ”في البَيْتِ عَمْرٍو“, until you say: ”وَعَمْرٍو في البَيْتِ“ (I passed by Zayd in the house, and by ʿAmr in the room).

zajjaj:72-72.t:
﴿قالَتْ يا ويْلَتى أألِدُ وأنا عَجُوزٌ﴾ — the muṣḥaf has ”يا ويْلَتى“ with yāʾ, and the reading is with alif, if you wish with tafkhīm (full open pronunciation), and if you wish with imāla (inclination toward e). The origin is ”يا ويْلَتِي“; the alif was substituted for the yāʾ and the kasra, because fatḥa and alif are lighter than yāʾ and kasra. Pausing on it without the hāʾ is permissible, but the preferred choice is to pause on it with the hāʾ: ”يا ويْلَتاهُ“.
As for the muṣḥaf, it is not to be contradicted, and one does not pause on it without the hāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense intended seems to be that, out of respect for the muṣḥaf's spelling, one should not pause on it with an added hāʾ, as the next clause shows]; if one pausing is compelled, he pauses without the hāʾ. As for the two hamzas after ”يا ويْلَتى“, there are three aspects in them:
if you wish, you pronounce the first fully and lighten the second, saying ”يا ويْلَتى أالِدُ“; if you wish — and this is the preferred choice — you lighten the first and lighten the second, saying ”يا ويْلَتى آلِدُ“; and if you wish, you pronounce both fully, saying ”أألِدُ“.
Full pronunciation of both hamzas is the position of Ibn Abī Isḥāq. ﴿وَهَذا بَعْلِي شَيْخًا﴾: the reading is the accusative, and so it is in the muṣḥaf agreed upon. It is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the accusative of the ḥāl here is among the subtle and obscure points of grammar. That is because when you say ”هَذا زَيْدٌ قائِمًا“ (this is Zayd, standing), if you intend to inform someone who does not know Zayd that he is Zayd, it is not permissible to say ”هَذا زَيْدٌ قائِمًا“, because [it would mean] he is Zayd only as long as he is standing,
and when he ceases standing he is not Zayd. You say ”هَذا زَيْدٌ قائِمًا“ only to someone who knows Zayd; then the alerting [sense of the demonstrative] governs the ḥāl, and the meaning is: "Pay attention to Zayd in the state of his standing", and "I point out to you Zayd in the state of his standing", because ”هَذا“ is a pointing to what is present. So the accusative is the correct way, as we have mentioned.
The nominative is permissible. Sībawayh and al-Khalīl held that the nominative is of four aspects. One of them is that you say ”هَذا زَيْدٌ قائِمٌ“, making Zayd nominative by ”هَذا“ and making ”قائِمٌ“ nominative as a second khabar (predicate), as though you said "he is standing" or "this is standing". You may also make Zayd and standing both predicates of ”هَذا“, making both nominative as predicates of ”هَذا“, as you say ”هَذا حُلْوٌ حامِضٌ“ (this is sweet-sour), meaning that it combines both tastes. You may make Zayd a badal (substitute) from ”هَذا“, as though you said ”زَيْدٌ قائِمٌ“. And you may make Zayd an explanation of ”هَذا“, as though you meant "this is standing", then made clear who he is by your saying "Zayd". These are four aspects.

zajjaj:74-74.t:
﴿فَلَمّا ذَهَبَ عَنْ إبْراهِيمَ الرَّوْعُ﴾ — ”اَلرَّوْعُ“ is fright, meaning his alarm when he found them strange as they did not eat of the calf. ”اَلرُّوْعُ“, with ḍamma on the rāʾ, is the soul; one says ”وَقَرَ ذَلِكَ في رُوعِي“ (that settled in my rūʿ), i.e. "in my soul and in my mind".
﴿وَجاءَتْهُ البُشْرى يُجادِلُنا في قَوْمِ لُوطٍ﴾ — ”يُجادِلُنا“ is the narration of a state that has passed (ḥikāyat ḥāl), because ”لَمّا“ is used in speech for something that has happened because of the happening of something else; you say ”لَمّا جاءَ زَيْدٌ جاءَ عَمْرٌو“ (when Zayd came, ʿAmr came). ”لَمّا جاءَ زَيْدٌ يَتَكَلَّمُ وعَمْرٌو“ [Translator's note: so in the source] is permissible, in two ways. One of them is that since ”إنْ“ [Translator's note: so in the source] is a condition for the future, the past [verb] occurring in it takes the sense of the future, as in ”إنْ جاءَ زَيْدٌ جِئْتُ“ (if Zayd comes, I will come).
The second way — which is the one I choose — is that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) for the narration of something that has passed. The meaning: "When the fright left Abraham and the glad tidings came to him, he set about (akhadha) disputing with Us concerning the people of Lot, and he began (aqbala) disputing with Us." ”أخَذَ“ and ”أقْبَلَ“ were not mentioned in the speech because in every speech addressed to an addressee there is the sense of ”أخَذَ“ and ”أقْبَلَ“ when you intend the narration of a state. For when you say ”قامَ زَيْدٌ“ (Zayd stood), you indicate a past act; and when you say ”أخَذَ زَيْدٌ يَقُولُ“ (Zayd set about saying), you indicate an extended state, for whose sake you mentioned ”أخَذَ“ and ”أقْبَلَ“. Likewise ”جَعَلَ زَيْدٌ يَقُولُ كَذا وكَذا“ (Zayd began saying such-and-such) and ”كَرَبَ يَقُولُ كَذا وكَذا“ (he was about to say such-and-such).
We have mentioned ”اَلْأوّاهُ“ elsewhere: it is the one who supplicates earnestly to Allah, humble in his supplication, compassionate, who sighs much (taʾawwuh) out of fear and apprehension over sins. It is related that his disputing concerning the people of Lot was that he said to the angels — when they had informed him that they were going to destroy them —: "Do you think, if there were fifty believers in it, would you destroy them along with them?!" — until he got down to five, and they said: "No." And Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿فَما وجَدْنا فِيها غَيْرَ بَيْتٍ مِنَ المُسْلِمِينَ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 36].
It is related that they were a great multitude; the most that has been related about them is that they were four thousand. ﴿يا إبْراهِيمُ أعْرِضْ عَنْ هَذا﴾ [Hūd: 76] — the meaning: "He disputed with Us, so We said: O Abraham, turn away from this." It is related that when the angels came to Abraham he was working in a piece of land of his, and every time he finished a dabra of the dibār — which are what are called mashārāt (garden plots) — he would plant his spade (bāla) [in the ground] and pray. So the angels said: "It is fitting that Allah should take Abraham as an intimate friend (khalīl)."

zajjaj:77-77.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَمّا جاءَتْ رُسُلُنا لُوطًا سِيءَ بِهِمْ﴾ — its meaning is: "their coming distressed him", because they sought his hospitality and he feared his people on their account. When he had walked with them a little, he said to them: "The people of this town are the worst of Allah's creation." The messengers had been charged not to destroy them until Lot testified against them three times.
Then he went on with them a little after that and repeated the words to them, then did that a third time, and they went on with him. ﴿سِيءَ بِهِمْ﴾: its origin is ”سُوِئَ بِهِمْ“, from ”اَلسُّوءُ“ (evil), except that the wāw was made quiescent and its kasra transferred to the sīn.
Whoever lightens the hamza says ”سِيَّ بِهِمْ“. ﴿وَضاقَ بِهِمْ ذَرْعًا﴾ — one says ”ضاقَ زَيْدٌ بِأمْرِهِ ذَرْعًا“ (Zayd was at his wits' end over his affair) when he finds no way out of what is hateful in that affair. ﴿وَقالَ هَذا يَوْمٌ عَصِيبٌ﴾, i.e. severe. When he had taken them in as guests, his wife — the evil old woman — went off and said to his people: "Lot has been visited by guests; I have never seen people fairer of face than them, nor sweeter of scent, nor cleaner of clothing."

zajjaj:78-78.t:
﴿وَجاءَهُ قَوْمُهُ يُهْرَعُونَ إلَيْهِ﴾, i.e. hastening in their coming. They sought to seduce him away from his guests and tried to open his door. The angels informed him that they were messengers of Allah and that his wicked people would not reach them. Lot said to them — when they sought his guests —: ﴿هَؤُلاءِ بَناتِي هُنَّ أطْهَرُ لَكم فاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ ولا تُخْزُونِ في ضَيْفِي﴾. It has been said that marriage was offered to them, as though he offered it to them if they would accept Islam. It has also been said: ”هَؤُلاءِ بَناتِي“ means the women of my nation, as though he said to them: marriage is purer for you. When they tried to open the door, Allah blotted out their eyes. Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿وَلَقَدْ راوَدُوهُ عَنْ ضَيْفِهِ فَطَمَسْنا أعْيُنَهُمْ﴾ [al-Qamar: 37]. And when he urged them to hasten the punishment, the messengers said to him: ﴿إنَّ مَوْعِدَهُمُ الصُّبْحُ ألَيْسَ الصُّبْحُ بِقَرِيبٍ﴾ [Hūd: 81].
﴿هُنَّ أطْهَرُ لَكُمْ﴾: the reading is with the nominative in ”أطْهَرُ“. It has been related from al-Ḥasan: ”هُنَّ أطْهَرَ لَكُمْ“, and from ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar. Sībawayh mentioned that Ibn Marwān committed a solecism (laḥn) in this by making it accusative. None of the Basrans and their followers permits the accusative of ”أطْهَرُ“, while others permit it. Those who permit it treat ”هُنَّ“ here as it is [used] with ”كانَ“: when they say ”هَؤُلاءِ بَناتِي أطْهَرَ لَكُمْ“, they permit ”هُنُّ أطْهَرَ لَكُمْ“, just as they permit ”كانَ زَيْدٌ هو أطْهَرَ مِن عَمْرٍو“ (Zayd was — he — purer than ʿAmr). But this is not on the level of ”كانَ“.
”هُوَ“, its dual and its plural may occur as an ʿimād (support pronoun) only where the speech is not complete without it [i.e. without the predicate], as in ”كانَ زَيْدٌ أخاكَ“ (Zayd was your brother), because they inserted ”هُمْ“ only to make known that the khabar (predicate) is indispensable and that it is not a ṣifa (adjective) of the first. But in the case of ”هَذا“ the speech is complete with its predicate: when you say ”هَذا زَيْدٌ“, it is a complete statement. If this were permissible, ”جاءَ زَيْدٌ هو أنْبَلُ مِن عَمْرٍو“ would be permissible.
The consensus of the grammarians, Kufan and Basran, is that ”قَدِمَ زَيْدٌ هو أنْبَلَ مِنكَ“ is not permissible until they make it nominative and say ”هُوَ أنْبَلُ مِنكَ“ (he is nobler than you). Moreover, those who read with the nominative are the readers of the great cities, and they are the majority. And al-Ḥasan read ”اَلشَّياطُونَ“, and ”اَلشَّياطُونَ“ is impossible in Arabic.
Some have said that the polytheists in that age were permitted to marry from among the Muslims.

zajjaj:81-81.t:
His saying: ﴿فَأسْرِ بِأهْلِكَ بِقِطْعٍ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ﴾, i.e. in a darkness of the night. It is said that the meaning of ”قِطْعٍ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ“ is a good portion [of it]; likewise ”مَضى عِنْكٌ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ“ and ”سِعْوٌ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ“ (a portion of the night has passed). It is read ”فَأسْرِ“, with the hamza pronounced, and it is read ”فاسْرِ“. One says ”أسْرَيْتَ، وسَرَيْتُ“ when I travel by night. The poet said:
؎سَرَيْتُ بِهِمْ حَتّى تَكِلَّ مَطِيُّهم وحَتّى الجِيادُ ما يُقَدْنَ بِأرْسانِ
(I travelled with them by night until their mounts grew weary, and until the steeds no longer needed to be led by halters.)
And al-Nābigha said:
؎أسْرَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ الجَوْزاءِ سارِيَةٌ ∗∗∗ تُزْجِي الشَّمالَ عَلَيْها جامِدُ البَرَدِ
(A night-cloud of Gemini travelled over them by night, the north wind driving upon it frozen hail.)
They have also related this verse with ”سَرَتْ“. And Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿سُبْحانَ الَّذِي أسْرى بِعَبْدِهِ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 1].
His saying: ﴿إلا امْرَأتَكَ﴾ — both the accusative and the nominative are permissible in it. Whoever read ”إلّا امْرَأتَكَ“ in the accusative, it is on the sense of "So travel by night with your family, except your wife"; whoever read with the nominative construed it on the sense of "and let none of you look back, except your wife".

zajjaj:82-82.t:
His saying: ﴿جَعَلْنا عالِيَها سافِلَها﴾ — it is said that Gabriel put his wing beneath it, then raised it to the sky until the inhabitants of the sky heard the barking of the dogs and the crowing of the cocks; then he turned it over upon them. ﴿وَأمْطَرْنا عَلَيْها حِجارَةً مِن سِجِّيلٍ مَنضُودٍ﴾ ﴿مُسَوَّمَةً عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ﴾ [Hūd: 83].
People have given several views on ”سِجِّيلٍ“. In the tafsīr it is that they were of jill (clay) and stones [Translator's note: i.e. from Persian sang (stone) and gil (clay)]. The people of language said: it is a Persian word Arabized, and the Arabs did not know it. My own view is that if this interpretation is correct, then it is Persian Arabized, because Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — mentioned these stones in the story of Lot's people, saying: ﴿لِنُرْسِلَ عَلَيْهِمْ حِجارَةً مِن طِينٍ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 33]; so it became clear to the Arabs what was meant by ”سِجِّيلٍ“.
And of the speech of the Persians there is no counting what the Arabs have Arabized, such as ”جامُوسٌ“ (buffalo) and ”دِيباجٌ“ (brocade); so I do not deny that this is among what has been Arabized. Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar ibn al-Muthannā said: its interpretation is "very hard"; and he said that the like of that is the poet's saying:
؎وَرَجْلَةٍ يَضْرِبُونَ البَيْضَ عَنْ عُرُضٍ ضَرْبًا تَواصَتْ بِهِ الأبْطالُ سِجِّينا
(And many a band on foot striking the helmets from the side, with blows that heroes enjoin upon one another — hard [sijjīn].)
The verse is by Ibn Muqbil; ”سِجِّينٌ“ and ”سِجِّيلٌ“ have one meaning.
Some said: ”سِجِّيلٌ“ is from ”أسْجَلْتُهُ“, i.e. I sent it loose, so it is as though they were sent loose upon them. Some said: ”مِن سِجِّيلٍ“ is from ”أسْجَلْتُ“ when I give, deriving it from ”اَلسَّجْلُ“, which is the [full] bucket. Al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās said:
؎مَن يُساجِلْنِي يُساجِلْ ماجِدًا ∗∗∗ يَمْلَأُ الدَّلْوَ إلى عَقْدِ الكَرَبْ
(Whoever vies with me bucket for bucket vies with a glorious man who fills the bucket up to the knot of the rope.)
It has also been said: ”مِن سِجِّيلٍ“ is like your saying "of what was recorded (sujjila)", i.e. "of what was written for them". This view, when explained, is the most solid of them, because in the Book of Allah the Exalted there is evidence for it.
He — Majestic and Mighty is He — said: ﴿كَلا إنَّ كِتابَ الفُجّارِ لَفي سِجِّينٍ﴾ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 7] ﴿وَما أدْراكَ ما سِجِّينٌ﴾ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 8] ﴿كِتابٌ مَرْقُومٌ﴾ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 9]. ”سِجِّيلٌ“ has the meaning of ”سِجِّينٌ“; so the meaning is that they were stones of those with which Allah — exalted is His praise — wrote that He would punish them. In my view this is the best of what has been said about it.
As for His saying ﴿مَنضُودٍ﴾ ﴿مُسَوَّمَةً عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ﴾ [Hūd: 83], its meaning [of manḍūd] is that they come one with another like rain. As for ”مُسَوَّمَةً عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ“, it is related from al-Ḥasan that they were marked with white and red. Others said: ”مُسَوَّمَةً“ means with a mark by which it is known that they are not of the stones of the people of this world, and by their mark it is known that they are among those with which Allah punished. ﴿وَما هي مِنَ الظّالِمِينَ بِبَعِيدٍ﴾ [Hūd: 83] — it has been said: they are not far from the wrongdoers of this nation.

zajjaj:84-84.t: ﴿وَإلى مَدْيَنَ أخاهم شُعَيْبًا﴾ — the meaning: We sent to the people of Madyan their brother Shuʿayb. ”أهْلِ“ (people) was omitted and ”مَدْيَنَ“ was put in its place. ”مَدْيَنُ“ is the name of the city or of the tribe, and therefore it is a diptote.

zajjaj:86-86.t: His saying: ﴿بَقِيَّتُ اللَّهِ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ﴾ — its meaning is: obedience to Allah is better for you, ﴿إنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾. Its meaning may also be: "the state of good that remains for you is better for you".

zajjaj:87-87.t: ﴿قالُوا يا شُعَيْبُ أصَلاتُكَ﴾ — and it is read ”أصَلَواتُكَ“ (your prayers) — ﴿تَأْمُرُكَ أنْ نَتْرُكَ ما يَعْبُدُ آباؤُنا﴾: this is evidence that they used to worship other than Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He. ﴿أوْ أنْ نَفْعَلَ في أمْوالِنا ما نَشاءُ﴾ — the meaning: "We have agreed among ourselves on short-changing." In the tafsīr it is that he forbade them to clip the dirhams, i.e. to break them. ﴿إنَّكَ لأنْتَ الحَلِيمُ الرَّشِيدُ﴾ — it has been said that this is an allusion (kināya) for their saying to him "You are the foolish, the ignorant"; and it has been said that they said this to him by way of mockery.

zajjaj:88-88.t:
His saying: ﴿قالَ يا قَوْمِ أرَأيْتُمْ إنْ كُنْتُ عَلى بَيِّنَةٍ مِن رَبِّي ورَزَقَنِي مِنهُ رِزْقًا حَسَنًا﴾ — the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) here is left out. The meaning: "If I am upon clear evidence from my Lord, shall I follow error?" The apodosis was left out because those addressed know the meaning. We have already met [instances] whose apodosis was left out because it is known, with their explanation in their places.
His saying: ﴿وَرَزَقَنِي مِنهُ رِزْقًا حَسَنًا﴾, i.e. lawful; it has also been said: ”رِزْقًا حَسَنًا“ is the obedience he was enabled to. ﴿وَما أُرِيدُ أنْ أُخالِفَكم إلى ما أنْهاكم عَنْهُ﴾, i.e. I do not forbid you something and then enter into it myself; I only choose for you what I choose for myself. The meaning of ”ما أُخالِفُكَ إلَيْهِ“ is: "I do not, by going against you, aim at committing it." ﴿إنْ أُرِيدُ إلا الإصْلاحَ ما اسْتَطَعْتُ﴾, i.e. as far as my capacity goes; and the extent of my capacity is conveying [the message] to you and warning you; I am not able to compel you to obedience. Then he said: ﴿وَما تَوْفِيقِي إلا بِاللَّهِ﴾, making known that neither he nor anyone else is able to obey except by Allah's enabling grace (tawfīq). The meaning of ”إلَيْهِ أُنِيبُ“ is: to Him I return.

zajjaj:89-89.t: ﴿وَيا قَوْمِ لا يَجْرِمَنَّكم شِقاقِي أنْ يُصِيبَكُمْ﴾ — the position of ”أنْ“ is accusative. The meaning: "Let not your enmity toward me earn you that the immediate punishment should strike you" ﴿مِثْلُ ما أصابَ قَوْمَ نُوحٍ أوْ قَوْمَ هُودٍ أوْ قَوْمَ صالِحٍ وما قَوْمُ لُوطٍ مِنكم بِبَعِيدٍ﴾. The destruction of Lot's people was the nearest of the destructions they knew, so it is as though he said to them: the admonition in Lot's people is near to you.

zajjaj:91-91.t: ﴿قالُوا يا شُعَيْبُ ما نَفْقَهُ كَثِيرًا مِمّا تَقُولُ وإنّا لَنَراكَ فِينا ضَعِيفًا﴾ — he was blind, and Ḥimyar call the blind man "weak" (ḍaʿīf). This is as one says ḍarīr (blind), i.e. one harmed (ḍurra) by the loss of his sight; and likewise he is kept back (kuffa) from moving about freely by the loss of his sight. ﴿وَلَوْلا رَهْطُكَ لَرَجَمْناكَ﴾, i.e. were it not for your kinsfolk we would have stoned you, i.e. killed you by stoning — and stoning is among the worst ways of killing. His kinsfolk were of their religion, and therefore they showed inclination toward them and honour for them.

zajjaj:92-92.t:
﴿قالَ يا قَوْمِ أرَهْطِي أعَزُّ عَلَيْكم مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾, i.e. you claim that you refrain from killing me out of regard for my kinsfolk, while Allah — Majestic and Mighty is He — is more worthy that His command be followed. ﴿واتَّخَذْتُمُوهُ وراءَكم ظِهْرِيًّا﴾, i.e. you have cast it behind your backs. The Arabs say of anyone who pays no heed to a matter: ”قَدْ جَعَلَ فُلانٌ الأمْرَ بِظَهْرِهِ“ (so-and-so has put the matter at his back). The poet said:
؎تَمِيمَ بْنَ قَيْسٍ لا تَكُونَنَّ حاجَتِي بِظَهْرٍ فَلا يَعْيا عَلَيَّ جَوابُها
(O Tamīm ibn Qays, let not my need be [cast] behind your back, so that its answer will not fail me.)

zajjaj:94-94.t: His saying — Majestic and Mighty is He —: ﴿وَأخَذَتِ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا الصَّيْحَةُ فَأصْبَحُوا في دِيارِهِمْ جاثِمِينَ﴾ — it is related that Gabriel gave a shout at them and they died in their places; so they became prostrate (jāthimīn), unable to move, having died.

zajjaj:95-95.t: ﴿كَأنْ لَمْ يَغْنَوْا فِيها﴾: as though they had never dwelt in it. One says ”غَنِينا بِالمَكانِ“ (we dwelt in the place) when we stay there. ﴿ألا بُعْدًا لِمَدْيَنَ﴾ — ”ألا“ is a particle with which speech is begun, and it is an alerting (tanbīh) of the one addressed. The meaning of ”بُعْدًا لِمَدْيَنَ“ is that they have been removed far from the mercy of Allah. It is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun); the meaning: Allah removed them far, so they became far, far indeed. The proof of that is ﴿كَما بَعِدَتْ ثَمُودُ﴾. Both ”بَعَدَتْ“ and ”بَعُدَتْ“ are permissible.

zajjaj:96-96.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أرْسَلْنا مُوسى بِآياتِنا﴾, i.e. with Our signs which point to the truth of his prophethood, ﴿وَسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ﴾, i.e. and a clear proof. The sulṭān (ruler) is called sulṭān only because he is Allah's proof in His earth. The derivation of ”اَلسُّلْطانُ“ is from ”اَلسَّلِيطُ“, and ”اَلسَّلِيطُ“ is what one lights with; from this oil is called ”سَلِيطٌ“.

zajjaj:97-97.t: ﴿إلى فِرْعَوْنَ ومَلَئِهِ﴾ — ”مَلْؤُهُ“ are the nobles of his people, who are full (milāʾ) of counsel and capability. ﴿فاتَّبَعُوا أمْرَ فِرْعَوْنَ وما أمْرُ فِرْعَوْنَ بِرَشِيدٍ﴾, i.e. they preferred blindness to guidance.

zajjaj:98-98.t:
﴿يَقْدُمُ قَوْمَهُ يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ﴾ — one says ”قَدَمْتُ القَوْمَ، أقْدُمُهُمْ، قَدْمًا، وقُدُومًا“ when I go ahead of them, i.e. "he will go ahead of them to the Fire". This is shown by His saying: ﴿فَأوْرَدَهُمُ النّارَ وبِئْسَ الوِرْدُ المَوْرُودُ﴾.
His saying: ﴿بِئْسَ الرِّفْدُ المَرْفُودُ﴾ [Hūd: 99] — everything you have made a support for something, and with which you have propped something up, you have rafadta it. One says ”عَمَدْتُ الحائِطَ“, ”أسْنَدْتُهُ“ and ”رَفَدْتُهُ“ (I propped up the wall) with one meaning. ”اَلْمَرْفَدُ“ is the large drinking-bowl.

zajjaj:100-100.t: His saying: ﴿مِنها قائِمٌ وحَصِيدٌ﴾, i.e. of the towns that were destroyed, [some are] standing, their walls having remained, like His saying: ﴿وَبِئْرٍ مُعَطَّلَةٍ وقَصْرٍ مَشِيدٍ﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 45]; and ”حَصِيدٌ“ is swallowed up [by the earth], namely that whose trace has been effaced.

zajjaj:101-101.t: His saying: ﴿وَما زادُوهم غَيْرَ تَتْبِيبٍ﴾ — its meaning is: nothing but causing loss. From it is His saying: ﴿تَبَّتْ يَدا أبِي لَهَبٍ﴾ [al-Masad: 1], i.e. they have lost.

zajjaj:103-103.t: His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ يَوْمٌ مَجْمُوعٌ لَهُ النّاسُ وذَلِكَ يَوْمٌ مَشْهُودٌ﴾ — so Allah — Mighty and Majestic is He — made known that He will bring creation to life and raise them on that day, and they will witness it.

zajjaj:105-105.t:
His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿يَوْمَ يَأْتِ لا تَكَلَّمُ نَفْسٌ إلا بِإذْنِهِ﴾ — what the grammarians prefer is ”يَوْمَ يَأْتِي لا تَكَلَّمُ نَفْسٌ إلّا بِإذْنِهِ“, with the yāʾ retained. What is in the muṣḥaf, and what the readers of the readings follow, is with kasra on the tāʾ without yāʾ. Hudhayl frequently use the dropping of these yāʾs.
Sībawayh and al-Khalīl mentioned that the Arabs say ”لا أدْرِ“ (I don't know), dropping the yāʾ and making do with the kasra, except that they hold that this is due to frequency of use. The better in grammar is retaining the yāʾ; but what I hold is following the muṣḥaf together with the consensus of the readers, because the reading is a sunna (followed practice).
Its like has come in the speech of the Arabs. This verse contains a question which the people of heresy in religion ask about more than anything. They say: why did He say ”يَوْمَ يَأْتِ لا تَكَلَّمُ نَفْسٌ إلّا بِإذْنِهِ“, and ﴿هَذا يَوْمُ لا يَنْطِقُونَ﴾ [al-Mursalāt: 35] ﴿وَلا يُؤْذَنُ لَهم فَيَعْتَذِرُونَ﴾ [al-Mursalāt: 36],
while He said in places where the Resurrection is mentioned: ﴿فَأقْبَلَ بَعْضُهم عَلى بَعْضٍ يَتَلاوَمُونَ﴾ [al-Qalam: 30], and said: ﴿يَوْمَ تَأْتِي كُلُّ نَفْسٍ تُجادِلُ عَنْ نَفْسِها﴾ [al-Naḥl: 111], and said: ﴿وَقِفُوهم إنَّهم مَسْؤُولُونَ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 24], and said: ﴿فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لا يُسْألُ عَنْ ذَنْبِهِ إنْسٌ ولا جانٌّ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 39]? We explain this according to what the early scholars of language — Muslims sound in their Islam — said. They said: His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَقِفُوهم إنَّهم مَسْؤُولُونَ﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 24]: Allah knows their deeds, but He asks them a question of rebuke and of making them acknowledge, in order to establish the proof against them.
His saying: ﴿فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لا يُسْألُ عَنْ ذَنْبِهِ إنْسٌ ولا جانٌّ﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 39], i.e. he is not asked in order that this be learned from him, because Allah knew their deeds before they did them. Likewise His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿لا يَنْطِقُونَ﴾ [al-Mursalāt: 35], i.e. they will not utter a proof that would avail them; they will only speak in acknowledgement of their sins, blaming one another, and throwing the sins on one another.
As for speaking and uttering a proof in their favour — no. This is as you say to one who addresses you at length while his address is empty of proof: "You have said nothing" and "You have uttered nothing". So one who speaks that in which there is no proof for him is called "not speaking", as He — Mighty and Majestic is He — said: ﴿صُمٌّ بُكْمٌ عُمْيٌ فَهم لا يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ [al-Baqara: 18], while they see and hear; but in that they do not accept, do not reflect on what they hear and do not take heed (yataʾattalūn) [Translator's note: so in the source], they are on the level of the deaf. The poet said:
؎أصَمُّ عَمّا ساءَهُ سَمِيعُ
(Deaf to what displeases him, [yet] hearing.)
This is a good view. Others said: that day is long, and has places, stations and halts; in some of them they are prevented from speaking, and in some speech is permitted them; this is indicated by ﴿لا تَكَلَّمُ نَفْسٌ إلا بِإذْنِهِ﴾. Both views are good and fine.

zajjaj:106-106.t: ﴿فَأمّا الَّذِينَ شَقُوا فَفي النّارِ لَهم فِيها زَفِيرٌ﴾ — [zafīr is] of the severest and ugliest groaning — ﴿وَشَهِيقٌ﴾: ”اَلشَّهِيقُ“ is severe groaning, raised very high. The people of language among the Basrans and the Kufans held that zafīr is like the beginning of the donkey's sound in braying, and shahīq like the end of its sound in braying.

zajjaj:107-107.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿إلا ما شاءَ رَبُّكَ﴾ — there are four views on it, two of them belonging to the people of language, Basrans and Kufans together. They said: the meaning is [as in] ”لَوْ كانَ مَعَنا رَجُلٌ إلّا زَيْدًا“ (if there were a man with us other than Zayd), i.e. "besides Zayd", and ”لَكَ عِنْدِي ألْفُ دِرْهَمٍ سِوى الألْفَيْنِ“ (you are owed a thousand dirhams by me besides the two thousand), and "except the two thousand that I owe". So the meaning on this view is: "abiding therein for the duration of the heavens and the earth, besides what your Lord wills of abiding and increase", just as you said "besides the two thousand that I owe".
They gave another view: "except what your Lord wills — and He does not will to bring them out of it", as you say: "I will do such-and-such, unless I will otherwise", and then you persist in that action while being able to do otherwise. The benefit of this speech, then, is that if He willed to bring them out He would be able to, but He has made known to us that they abide forever. These two are among the positions of the people of language.
And two other views. Some said: when they are gathered and raised, they are within the conditions of the Resurrection, so the exception is made from the abiding to the extent of their standing for the reckoning. The meaning: "abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except for the length of their standing for the reckoning". There is a fourth view on it: that the exception falls on their having therein zafīr and shahīq, except what your Lord wills of kinds of punishment that have not been mentioned.
Likewise the people of Paradise have the bliss that has been mentioned, and they have what has not been mentioned of what your Lord wills. This is indicated — and Allah knows best — by ﴿عَطاءً غَيْرَ مَجْذُوذٍ﴾ [Hūd: 108], i.e. not cut off. Al-Nābigha said:
؎تَجُذُّ السُّلُوقِيَّ المُضاعَفَ نَسْجُهُ وتُوقِدُ بِالصُّفّاحِ نارَ الحُباحِبِ
(They cut through the Salūqī [mail] of doubled weave, and strike from the stone slabs sparks like fireflies.)
He is describing swords, and that they cut through coats of mail.

zajjaj:109-109.t: His saying — Mighty and Majestic is He —: ﴿وَإنّا لَمُوَفُّوهم نَصِيبَهم غَيْرَ مَنقُوصٍ﴾, i.e. We shall pay them in full what falls to them of good or evil.

zajjaj:111-111.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإنَّ كُلا لَمّا لَيُوَفِّيَنَّهم رَبُّكَ أعْمالَهُمْ﴾ — it has been read with the nūn doubled and lightened, and it has been read ”لَما“ with the mīm lightened and ”لَمّا“ with it doubled. As for doubling ”إنَّ“ with the accusative, that is according to the pattern of ”إنَّ“. As for lightening it while leaving the accusative as it is, that is because ”إنَّ“ resembles the verb, so when the doubling is removed from it the government remains as it is. As for lightening ”لَمّا“, that is the correct way and the analogy: the lām of ”لَمّا“ is the lām of ”إنَّ“, and ”ما“ is redundant (zāʾida), emphasizing, changing neither the meaning nor the government. As for the doubling in ”لَمّا“, some grammarians held that its meaning is ”لَمَن ما“; then the nūn was changed into mīm, so three mīms came together, and one of them — the middle one — was dropped, leaving ”لَمّا“.
This view is nothing, because ”مَن“ may not be dropped, since it is a noun of two letters. But regarding the doubling there are two views. One of them is related from al-Māzinī: al-Māzinī held that its origin is ”لَما“ and then the mīm was doubled. This view is also nothing, because particles such as ”رُبَّ“ and what resembles them are lightened, but we do not make heavy what consists of two letters; so this is refuted.
Some gave a view other than which nothing is permissible — and Allah knows best —: that ”لَمّا“ is in the sense of ”إلّا“ (except), as you say ”سَألْتُكَ لَمّا فَعَلْتَ كَذا وكَذا“ and ”إلّا فَعَلْتَ كَذا“ (I ask you [by Allah], do nothing but such-and-such). Its like is: ﴿إنْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ لَمّا عَلَيْها حافِظٌ﴾ [al-Ṭāriq: 4], its meaning being ”إلّا“. The interpretation of the lām with the light ”إنْ“ is only the interpretation of negation and affirmation: when you say ”إنْ زَيْدًا لَعالِمٌ“, ”إنْ“ is ”ما“ (not), but the lām entered upon it so that the negated would not resemble the affirmed. So the doubled [inna], by the entry of the lām upon it, takes the sense of the light [in] when the lām enters upon it.
On this basis ”إنْ“ that governs the accusative came; so it is possible that ”إنْ“ which governs the accusative — inasmuch as the lām entered upon it just as it entered upon ”إنْ“ that does not govern the accusative — has had ”لَمّا“ enter upon it, and ”إلّا“ enter upon it. So the speech, in singling out the affirmation for it, became like that from which everything other than what is mentioned after ”لَمّا“ is denied, and to which what comes after ”لَمّا“ is affirmed. So on this pattern you say ”إنَّ كُلَّهم لَمّا يُحِبَّنِي“, whose meaning comes back to the meaning of ”ما كُلُّهم إلّا يُحِبُّنِي“ (all of them do nothing but love me).
Likewise ”إنْ كُلًّا لَمّا يُحِبُّنِي“ is permissible, parallel to ”إنْ كُلًّا لَمّا يُحِبُّنِي“ [Translator's note: so in the source, the same phrase repeated; one of the two was presumably meant to be with ”إنَّ“], so ”لَمّا“ entered as affirming, just as the lām entered as affirming, and the interpretation of the sentence became that of the negated and affirmed. Sībawayh and all the Basrans reported that ”لَمّا“ is used in the sense of ”إلّا“. ”إنَّ كُلًّا لَمّا لَيُوَفِّيَنَّهُمْ“ is also permissible, meaning "Indeed, all — He will surely pay them in full, all together (lammā = jamʿan)", because the meaning of al-lamm is gathering; one says ”لَمَمْتُ الشَّيْءَ، ألُمُّهُ، لَمًّا“ when I gather it. As for their saying ”لَمَّ اللَّهُ شَعَثَكَ“, its interpretation is: "May Allah gather for you what removes your dishevelment."

zajjaj:114-114.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَأقِمِ الصَّلاةَ طَرَفَيِ النَّهارِ وزُلَفًا مِنَ اللَّيْلِ﴾ — the two ends of the day are its morning and its evening; the prayer of the two ends of the day is the dawn prayer, ẓuhr and ʿaṣr. ﴿وَزُلَفًا مِنَ اللَّيْلِ﴾ — ”وَزُلُفًا مِنَ اللَّيْلِ“ is also permissible, with ḍamma on the zāy and the lām. It is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), as you say: ”حَيِّنا طَرَفَيِ النَّهارِ، وأوَّلَ اللَّيْلِ“ (visit us at the two ends of the day and at the beginning of the night). The meaning of ”زُلَفًا مِنَ اللَّيْلِ“ is the prayer near the beginning of the night. ”زُلَفًا“ is the plural of ”زُلْفَةً“; by the zulaf of the night are meant maghrib and the later ʿishāʾ.
﴿إنَّ الحَسَناتِ يُذْهِبْنَ السَّيِّئاتِ﴾, i.e. these prayers expiate the sins between them; and this confirms what is in the report about the prayers expiating sins. ”اَلزُّلُفُ“ is singular, like ”اَلْحُلُمُ“, and it may be a plural of ”زَلِيفٍ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ“, so that it would be like ”اَلْقَرِيبُ“ and ”اَلْقُرْبُ“; but ”اَلزُّلَفُ“ is better as a plural, and I do not know that ”زَلِيفًا“ is used of the night.

zajjaj:116-116.t: His saying: ﴿أُولُو بَقِيَّةٍ﴾ — its meaning is: "possessors of discernment"; and its meaning may be: "possessors of obedience". The meaning of ”اَلْبَقِيَّةُ“, when you say ”فُلانٌ في بَقِيَّةٍ“, is: "there is excellence in him in that for which one is praised". ﴿إلا قَلِيلا مِمَّنْ أنْجَيْنا مِنهُمْ﴾ is a disjunctive exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ); the meaning: but a few of those We saved among them, of those who forbade corruption. ﴿واتَّبَعَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا ما أُتْرِفُوا فِيهِ﴾ — its meaning: they followed that by which luxury and comfort would last for them, and inclined toward this world, and did not accept anything that would diminish their luxury, whether in earning or in deed.

zajjaj:117-117.t: ﴿وَما كانَ رَبُّكَ لِيُهْلِكَ القُرى بِظُلْمٍ وأهْلُها مُصْلِحُونَ﴾ — it may be [in the sense of] "Your Lord would not destroy anyone while wronging him", as He said: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَظْلِمُ النّاسَ شَيْئًا﴾ [Yūnus: 44]. Its meaning may also be: "Your Lord would not destroy the towns — meaning the people of the towns — for wrongdoing while their people deal with one another with fairness."
